Why Black Friday and Cyber Monday Are Bad Days to Impulse Buy Electronics

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.
  • It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.
  • Some Cyber Monday deals are still live, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Some Cyber Monday deals are still live, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Follow our live blog to stay up-to-date on the best sales we find.

Browse our editors’ picks for a curated list of our favorite sales on laptops, fitness tech, appliances, and more.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Industry observers note that not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

According to recent reports, when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be mentioned for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Recent findings suggest that price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

Sources indicate that in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Recent findings suggest that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Recent findings suggest that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

According to recent reports, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

According to recent reports, black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

  • According to the organization, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple today declared that App Store prices for apps and In-App Purchases will be adjusted in five countries starting December 3, following changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates. Here are the details.

In a newly introduced post published on its developer portal, Apple today unveiled a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the organization, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple mentioned that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Apple added that a new “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and update their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, the company’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple this week revealed the additional Siri AI usage you’ll get if you have an iCloud+ subscription. This ranges from doubled limits for a 200GB proposal to 20 times for a 12TB plan.

However, the company’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

According to recent reports, apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time. However, it did list the proportional increases you get with paid iCloud prepares.

It has been revealed that however, tucked away in the small print in the manufacturer’s support document are some exclusions. One of them is no surprise: EU countries.

In a recent development, siri AI isn’t available at all in the EU due to Apple’s perception of potential antitrust concerns. Essentially, Apple believes that if it rolls out Siri AI there, it will be required to give competing AI services the same level of access to its devices. But three other countries are specifically excluded:.

Apple gives no explanation, simply saying:.

Increased access to Siri AI with iCloud+ is subject to Siri AI availability and is not available in Brazil, the EU, UK, or South Korea.

However, I have a strong suspicion about the reason.

What all three countries have in common is that they’ve taken a strong antitrust stance with Apple on a number of occasions over a range of challenges.

Industry observers note that it may be that Apple has genuine concerns about how regulators might respond if they effectively throw in free access to increased Siri AI usage. The company may fear that this would be viewed as anti-competitive by implicitly disadvantaging other AI services.

A less charitable take would be that Apple is firing a warning shot across the bows of these countries, seeking to communicate that there are consequences for what it views as attacks on its ecosystem. If customers are angered by missing out, Apple might be hoping that these feelings would be directed at regulators rather than the iPhone maker.

What’s your take? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

According to one report, Liverpool have the opportunity to snap up a full-back from a fellow European giant for a modest amount.

Despite the Barcelona loanee’s fine form, Jamie Carragher has implored his former club to move for a full-back in January if the right opportunity arises, and there might just be another one from Camp Nou.

As reported by Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, the LaLiga champions are prepared to sanction an exit for Alejandro Balde amid interest from Liverpool, with Barca head coach Hansi Flick indicating that the 23-year-old isn’t part of his prepares.

His representative Jorge Mendes has reportedly held talks with the Merseyside club to inform them of the conditions surrounding a potential deal for the player, who’s viewed by Anfield chiefs as an ‘attractive option’.

The agent is understood to have communicated a valuation of €40m (£33m) to prospective suitors, and that figure would apply whether the deal is structured as a permanent transfer or a loan arrangement with a purchase option.

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even though Balde has been overtaken by Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo in the left-back pecking order at Barcelona, Liverpool might still feel that the price point apparently quoted by Mendes would represent something of a bargain for the 23-year-old.

Catalan columnist Javier Miguel has previously hailed some ‘spectacular’ performances from the Spain international (AS), and an analysis from The Athletic highlighted his aptitude for taking on opposition full-backs whilst marauding along the left flank.

He’s also renowned for his pace, with his former agent Junior Minguella describing him as a ‘bullet’, and Flick previously spoke of how the Spain international strives to ‘get better every day’ (The Athletic).

If Kostas Tsimikas were to depart at the end of his contract next summer – certainly not an implausible scenario – then Liverpool would need to add left-back competition for Milos Kerkez, and Barcelona’s apparent readiness to offload Balde could play into our hands.

Recent findings suggest that considering the success we’ve had so far with Araujo, FSG might just be inclined to sound out the Catalan giants about potentially adding another full-back option from Flick’s squad in 2027. This could be an intriguing one to watch over the coming months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Sources indicate that finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A set of major tech outages in close succession is leading some to speculate that they are connected, and that the US is under systemic attack by a hostile state.

All the evidence suggests otherwise, with individual explanations for each of them – and the White House is now saying as much in a bid to put fears to rest ….

Whether there was or wasn't a cyber attack, I wouldn't believe a single word from the White House.

On Thursday, a widespread Microsoft 365 outage ran into the following day when two unrelated issues coincided. Friday saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centers. On Monday, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Finally, yesterday saw many Apple services offline, with retail stores also affected.

The Apple outage doesn’t appear to have been significant enough to have reached the administration’s radar, but CBS News reports secretary of state Marco Rubio saying the others are unrelated.

According to recent reports, “The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These challenges that we’ve seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another,” Rubio said […].

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”.

The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

Sources indicate that democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also remarked on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

Warner went on to say that the ability of AI systems to find vulnerabilities at “unprecedented speed” does, however, mean companies and government agencies alike need to be ready to patch vulnerabilities immediately.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today.
  • When MacPaw introduced Moonlock on the Mac, the manufacturer described its fresh app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.
  • According to recent reports, in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw introduced Moonlock on the Mac, the manufacturer described its fresh app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

According to recent reports, in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Consumers can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

It has been revealed that beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that reveals where apps are sending data and lets customers block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the tech giant says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping customers improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets consumers quickly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

As MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, people can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

“When we launched Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Check out Moonlock for iPhone on the App Store.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aqara has confirmed the global launch of six new smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the tech giant describes as “spatial intelligence.”.

The latest lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization ….

All of the new products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the upcoming products support spatial intelligence.

This enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

It has been revealed that its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

Industry observers note that you might initially struggle to spot the latest products in the firm’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

In a recent development, pricing ranges from $24 for new light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

  • It has been revealed that VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

It has been revealed that VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial upgrade.

On Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Industry observers note that colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I n December, Gustavo Dudamel will make his much-anticipated return to conduct the Los Angeles Philharmonic for a string of dates. It’s the first time he will head back to his former home of nearly 20 years since beginning his tenure as the Upcoming York Philharmonic’s Music and Artistic Director. Given the multiple standing ovations and chants of “Gustavo” that resonated through the Hollywood Bowl during his final LA Phil bow in late August, his arrival will be a much welcome one.

It has been revealed that alongside his trip back to the West Coast, Rolling Stone can exclusively announce a documentary about Dudamel and the LA Phil will premiere on Dec. 7 coinciding with his concerts at Walt Disney Hall on Dec. 4, 5, and 6. The documentary, titled Symphony of a Thousand, is described as “Set during challenging times in L.A., the film encapsulates Dudamel’s philosophy on how music can create connection and community in an increasingly fractured world.”.

It has been revealed that the Jennifer Tiexiera-directed film, produced by Brad Pitt’s Strategy B Entertainment, features footage from Dudamel and the LA Phil’s pair of performances at 2025’s Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, where they made history as the first major orchestra to perform a full set at the massive event. It features Dave Grohl,  LL Cool J, Cynthia Erivo, Natasha Bedingfield, Becky G, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, and Zedd. Kevin Macdonald serves as the executive producer, with producers Jeremy Kleiner, Dede Gardner, and Chloe Mamelok.

Industry observers note that landmark pop culture moments like this have peppered the course of Dudamel’s trailblazing career. And he wasn’t about to go (east) quietly. His final nights helming the LA Phil culminated in a weekend at the Bowl that featured the Foo Fighters and other pop luminaries, concerts that doubled as a benefit for his home country of Venezuela. A conversation at the Grammy Museum followed.

“I met Gustavo at a party about 12 years ago, and I fell in love with him. As a heterosexual man, it confused me,” Coldplay’s Chris Martin affectionately jokes when joining Dudamel and LA Phil onstage during the benefit concert for Venezuela finale. “And I realized it wasn’t so much sexual as musical in the way I just wanted to cuddle him forever. And we’ve been musically cuddling ever since.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Industry observers note that trailing Dudamel during his final full-time week in L.A., that sentiment carries through to every interaction. At the closed final rehearsal on a Sunday morning in August, camera crews swirl around as two women busily work to notate the score, and a handful of onlookers from the team at the Bowl gather to take in the moment in the blazing heat. There’s a hushed reverence knowing an era is coming to an end, but also smiles abound, particularly from Dudamel who warmly hugs old friends as they join him onstage.

As he conducts, he throws the full weight of his body in a stance both graceful and animated — like a kid at his first dance. His baton alights in the air and comes down, and the orchestra responds, while he swoops and sways to the music. “5/4 pum pum,” Dudamel instructs as they run through one composition. Later, Meme del Real from Café Tacvba takes the stage to rehearse the poignant “Eras.” Lasso follows with an a cappella of “En Otra Vida.”.

It’s the morning after their phenomenal performance with Foo Fighters, which marked the band’s first-ever set at the Hollywood Bowl. That pairing is not an unusual one for Dudamel, though. He’s made a name for himself breaking down perceived traditional genre boundaries in his 17 years at the Bowl, where he’s collaborated with an array of artists, including LL Cool J, Christina Aguilera, and Beck, who later at the finale concert performs “Ride Lonesome.” Beck’s dad, celebrated arranger-composer David Campbell, also attends the final rehearsal. It has been revealed that “If I reflect about how I feel, yes, I feel exhausted,” Dudamel tells Rolling Stone with a smile when we meet at the Grammy Museum a couple of days later. “Every day a rehearsal, every day a concert. Next day a different program, another concert.” It’s been a nonstop whirlwind, but it’s also been a time “full of beauty,” he states.

According to recent reports, “I have the chance to dive inside of all of that amount of talent — because it’s not only the soloists that play with me; it’s all that orchestra, that 100 musicians that are there, that I have shared 17 years of my life with them, and of course it doesn’t finish,” he continues. “This goes to eternity because when you develop something that is so deep and so powerful as developing an identity through music, it’s the biggest privilege … Every single note, every single second that I have the chance to share, or people share with me, that is a privilege to have the chance to work with all of these people and to create all of this environment.”.

In a recent development, if there are a couple of overarching words to describe Dudamel, they would be magnetic charm. When we arrive at the Grammy Museum a few hours before his event, several people rush him to ask for selfies, to which he happily obliges before he’s rapidly ushered into the building. People from the music world and beyond appear drawn to him, not only for the music he helms and the open environment he’s created around it, but also for his altruism.

At intermission during Dudamel’s Hollywood Bowl finale, Coldplay’s Martin heads backstage to rehearse with YOLA, the youth orchestra inspired by Dudamel’s own experience coming up in El Sistema, the publicly-funded National Network of Youth and Children Orchestras of Venezuela. (It was there while discovering music technique that “I saw the immense and infinite possibilities of all kinds of music,” Dudamel claims.) Martin asks each child their name before leading them through a warm-up and taking to the piano. He vamps his lyrics to “Viva La Vida” before the choir comes in with the buoyant Oh-oh-oh bridge. “Absolutely fantastic,” Martin tells the students. He reminds them: “Remember when we’re out there onstage, this is our band … We’re doing this together.” Later onstage, they deliver their spine-tingly performance, which prompts a crowd-wide sing-along.

Recent findings suggest that YOLA, which provides free instruments and education to create social change through music, is a vital part of Dudamel’s legacy and his north star. “I grew up not in an environment of conservatory, rigid. No,” he indicates. “It was music as a tool of social transformation — that is El Sistema. And of course, for me, opening spaces for young people to have access to music as a tool for them to have beauty, to have creativity, to have empathy, creating together — that is for me the most key thing. And [as] artistic institutions, we have to do that … for people to see the transforming power of music.

“When you have this chance to transform your life, creating harmony, creating beauty together — when you go out as a citizen, you behave differently because you see the real dimension of connection that goes beyond any material thing, any ideological point of view, and then you are connected through the empathy of human being and doing things beautiful for others.”.

As for his hopes to bring a similar program to Upcoming York and beyond, he believes it’s imperative. “We don’t have the chance in this world to contemplate, to really see each other, to create something that requires discipline, but at the same time joy together. When you are doing music, in an orchestra, in a choir, and you feel that first moment that you create harmony and that you are part of something beautiful and powerful, that enhances your spirit. I think that is the way for our kids to be inspired, especially in the chaotic but beautiful, in the only world that we have. So we have to create more spaces like this.”.

According to recent reports, as a longtime champion of crossover collaborations, Dudamel attracts artists across genres and disciplines, but a recent team-up came by way of an unusual source, via actor Bradley Cooper, who is a mutual friend of Dudamel’s and Stella Hopkins. Hopkins began sharing scores with Dudamel, which were composed by her husband, actor Anthony Hopkins. It led to them working on an album.

Sources indicate that “The thing about musicians is that they, unlike actors, they don’t have that ego,” Anthony Hopkins tells Rolling Stone of working with Dudamel. The pair met up at the Grammy Museum to talk about their collaboration on Hopkins’ debut classical album, Life Is a Dream. Dudamel conducted London’s Philharmonia Orchestra for the project, which comprises work Hopkins has composed over the course of more than six decades.

During his Venezuelan benefit show, Dudamel and LA Phil performed Hopkins’ “Stella Aria,” a moving ode to the actor’s wife, which featured a beautiful solo from Venezuelan cellist Gregorio Nieto at the concert.

According to recent reports, “It is a great honor and a privilege because he actually endorsed my music,” claims Hopkins. “I mean, I’m always filled with self-doubts as we all are … I have no theoretical, technical, musical training as such — everything is instinctive from childhood. So, naturally in me is the — ‘do I, is this good enough?,’ But when I sat there and Gustavo got up onto the podium to conduct the massive orchestra there, and I was astounded as the sound came out. He’s playing my music. Did I write that?’”.

Dudamel has a knack for making artists feel comfortable in new situations as his next act in New York illustrates — it has begun, unsurprisingly, with rave reviews. In September, his premiere debut with the New York Philharmonic at Radio City Music Hall drew the kind of rock star lineup one would expect from Dudamel. Hosted by Liev Schreiber, it featured Lizzo, St. Vincent, and Joaquina. “The Philharmonic plays for Dudamel with visible investment and enthusiasm,” a New York Times review of his first week’s New York concerts reads. “Its members haven’t looked this happy onstage in years. Either he inspires them, or his starry arrival has lifted their morale. Or both. Leaker Ice Universe says Apple is at the moment developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20. We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical new design with an all-glass appearance.

Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product ….

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

Recent findings suggest that ice Universe says that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.

Apple is currently developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of new devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

Sources indicate that we’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report notes the bezels are around 1mm thick.

The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

According to recent reports, we yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.

Latest Update: What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most important tech organization in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy.
  • In a recent development, at least, that’s the simple version of the story.
  • Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, claims Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most important tech organization in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy. The most valuable tech in the world — Huang’s super-powered computer chips — are smuggled into China or installed into data centers connected to America’s greatest rival. Above it all, the possibility of a super-intelligent AI, a true artificial mind, looms — and its creator will be positioned to rule the world.

In a recent development, at least, that’s the simple version of the story. But the real picture of the great geopolitical AI race is both more complex and more unbelievable than the tale of spies and smuggling that’s playing out in the press right now. China wants the U.S.’s chips — that much is clear. But why? And what can our only real rival power actually do with them? To answer this, Rolling Stone spoke with two experts in the Chinese tech sector, who pulled back the curtain on what the superpower actually wants when it comes to AI — and why it’s willing to use sex, smuggling and lies to get there.

Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, claims Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.

It has been revealed that the first is as a straight race to one goal: creating a truly intelligent AI that surpasses human intelligence in all general tasks and can improve itself autonomously. In the industry, this is known as AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence. This point of view holds that the first country or organization to achieve true AGI will have an earth-shattering advantage over any competition in economics, war, medicine, and technology. Basically, it sets the world of AI up as a winner-take-all race. Many U.S. officials — including, at times, Trump himself — have made this argument, alongside many of the private sector CEOs actually working on the technology.

According to recent reports, “If you start with that assumption, then the effort to slow down China is nearly existential,” Chan states. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The biggest advantage the U.S. has is Nvidia’s chips. The most powerful computer chips in the world are made by one facility in Taiwan, using incredibly complex and rare machines manufactured by one firm in the Netherlands. It is a process so detailed and scientifically complex that it might as well be magic. Other companies can make chips, of course, but none of them can make chips as well as the single manufacturing company in Taiwan that Nvidia and most of the U.S. tech giants use. AI companies need these chips, and these chips alone, to run the most advanced AI models — which is why the U.S. has done a lot to limit China’s access to them, setting export controls on who Nvidia can sell their chips to and which countries they can be shipped into.

Industry observers note that because of this constraint, the Chinese don’t really see AI the same way as most of the U.S. industry does.

Instead of an existential threat, Chan says, the second way to look at AI is a very powerful technology that will not necessarily lead to some massive strategic advantage for the first team past the AGI post. That makes the AI race a longer-term game, decided more by which power can holistically incorporate the advances of super-computing into its society and economy, which China has largely focused on doing.

According to recent reports, “What we’re kind of seeing unfold in the future is two different markets,” noted Kenton Thibaut, a China expert at the Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab. The U.S. is focused on “frontier” systems — the absolute cutting-edge AI, powered by their chip advantage — while China is supplying “near frontier” technology that hits different parts of the market for AI technology. In China, Thibaut said, AI is viewed as a “general purpose” technology that should be harnessed for practical use as quickly as possible, rather than a more conceptual race to the furthest frontier. Related Content Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire Trump States He ‘Can’t Speak To’ Whether Russia is a Friend to America Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi Your Favorite THC Drinks Are About to Be Illegal.

Industry observers note that “All of the [Chinese] policies and major policy pronouncements and planning around AI have to do with ‘How do we make this useful in society?’” Thibaut stated. “I haven’t seen anything like that in the US.”.

According to recent reports, “[China’s] version of winning is being able to benefit the most from AI,” Chan says. “Integrate it in their economy, automate their factories, speed up drug discovery, et cetera. [They want it to] help them win across all these other domains, rather than this singular focus on achieving AGI.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a philosophical difference that is fueled by the physical constraints that the Chinese tech sector faces. The U.S. has access to more computing power than any other nation, allowing them to push the envelope. Companies like Anthropic have asked the U.S. government to regulate them more, fearful that their AI models will run out of control. In China, these discussions are scarce, Thibaut says, because the hardware they’re working with basically makes them moot — and the Chinese government is predisposed to prevent any societal disruptions. Instead, Chinese AI firms are usually focused on doing more with less — creating working, practical products and applications of AI that get the most out of whatever computing power they can harness.

In a recent development, and in some cases, that’s where the spies come in. The Nvidia honeypot scandal was largely controversial because it included a woman who ran a Singaporean front tech giant that set up data centers in Southeast Asia stocked with Taiwan-made super-chips, and then leased the use of those chips to Chinese companies. Chan refers to this loophole, and the broader Chinese project of getting their hands on American tech, as a “bridge” to the country’s real goal: separating themselves from the Western “tech stack,” while still retaining competitive computing power. Eventually, Chan says, China wants to have its own version of the super-manufacturers in Taiwan, its own version of the very best chips — but until then, it has to use more subtle methods to get what it wants.

Recent findings suggest that “If they want to keep pace today, they do still need access to Nvidia chips now,” Chan says. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

Some parts of the U.S. government may be helping them achieve that. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik had been very lax with Nvidia and Huang personally, allowing the firm to continue selling to companies that the U.S. knew were linked with China. While Trump has mentioned he views AI as a winner-take-all race, Reuters reported that his administration also signed off on the sale of 900,000 AI chips to Chinese companies in one six-month period, and his own AI Czar David Sacks has explicitly advocated for selling more chips directly to China.

China, then, has allies to go along with its spies — and it seems that one way or another, it’s getting all the chips it needs.

Catherine, the Princess of Wales will discuss her cancer battle in an upcoming documentary special that will raise money for the hospital that treated her.

Heal: A Princess of Wales Story will air November 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC. The documentary follows Kate Middleton as she reflects on her cancer battle while completing the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the span of 24 hours — this past June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the hospital where she was treated; proceeds from the distribution of Heal will also benefit Royal Marsden.

“Cancer does change you. It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” the Princess of Wales says in the trailer.

“It’s clear we’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone. Things can renew and grow. After it is through pain that we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that.”.

The news of Middleton’s initial diagnosis was disclosed to the public in March 2024, following an abdominal surgery in January. In a video statement, Middleton mentioned, “At the time, it was thought that my condition was non-cancerous,” referring to her surgery. “The surgery was successful, however, tests after the operation on cancer had been present,” she added. The Making of My Chemical Romance’s ‘The Black Parade’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade.
  • Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by newly introduced music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade. It was Tommy in a white belt and eyeliner, vastly expanding the band’s sonic palette beyond the punk-thrash of their first two albums. It felt like the beginning of what should have been a long, ambitious latest phase of My Chem’s career, but instead, they released the underrated Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys in 2010 and broke up three years later.

Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by newly introduced music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a latest vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut. That album’s producer, Rob Cavallo (who also worked on much of Green Day‘s discography, among many other projects) joined Rolling Stone by Zoom for an in-depth look at the making of a 21st-century rock masterpiece.

What did My Chem first play for you that got you excited to be involved in this album?They were interviewing other guys as well, but I’ll never forget, ’cause it was so freezing cold in Newly introduced York, and we went to SIR, and they played me a few things. But the one that blew my mind was “Mama.” When I heard that, I remember just jumping off the couch just going, “Oh, my God, you guys. That is so great and original,” and you could tell it was part of a deeper picture of something, even though I was new to the band. It felt notable to me right away that this band was existing on a higher conceptual level.

That song sounds like the Doors version of “Alabama Song.” It’s very un-punk at first, and then it kicks into the—The heavy part, right. Yeah, I kinda likened it in a weird way rhythmically to the Doors. I was also thinking of [the Rolling Stones’] “Mother’s Little Helper.” Almost like you could see the Cossacks-style Russian dancing to it. It’s like this sort of head-bopping thing that just felt very edgy, and very anti-establishment rock in a weird way. It was definitely like the we-don’t-give-a-fuck kind of rock. It has been revealed that but then there was this story in there. I was like, “What is this guy going on about? What is happening here? This is heavy stuff.” So that’s why I jumped up off the couch on that song.

And of course, a lot of the record at that point had not been written. And then I got this call and they stated, “Meet us at this steakhouse near SIR.” And I remember walking there and I thought my legs were gonna freeze off. And then we got in and we had the greatest dinner ever, and they said, “All right, you wanna be our producer?” I said, “Yeah, I do.” And that was it. They decided a couple hours after the first meeting.

It has been revealed that do you think your enthusiasm put it over the top for them? Obviously it couldn’t have hurt that you had just done American Idiot, which had similar levels of ambition.I think I was told that they liked what I said about the music, and they probably liked that I had done two records that I think stood out in their minds. Yeah, I had just done American Idiot, which was of course really major and was working, and I think they liked that. And then I think the other record they mentioned was Jawbreaker, Dear You, which is a band and an album that had an infamous history of being a dismal failure, in a way, commercially when it first came out.

But also then received its just deserts many years later, in the fact that it was now considered one of the seminal emo records of all time. And of course, we all know the history about how the band got back together and then all of a sudden on one show there were 60,000 people singing every word to every song on that record. But at the same time we also know that Kurt Cobain was, like, one of their biggest supporters — they were opening for Nirvana. So it was kinda cool. How did My Chem define their ambitions on that first day?It wasn’t necessarily something that we actually talked about. I think Gerard [Way] had it in his mind, but a lot of it happened when we went into this place called the Paramour. The band was looking for a place where they could live and work and write.

A sort of haunted mansion, apparently.Oh, it was haunted all right. Crazy stuff was happening all the time. You could just feel the vibes of the insanity that was happening — doors closing by themselves, and probably the eeriest hallway. To this day, I still remember that hallway going down to where the bedrooms were on the top floor, and it just looked like you were in the scariest movie. And the coat of arms and the polar bear, the stuffed polar bear, all the weird stuff that was just everywhere.

And it was also kinda freezing in there. It was such an old building that we had to bring in space heaters, and so a lot of the writing actually ended up taking place over a couple of months in that particular space. And Mikey [Way] eventually, as you probably heard, he had to move out. He couldn’t take it after a while. It was just too scary.

But we had a lot of fun there, and we got a lot of the work done. So the record, I would say, was probably 90 percent written by the time, or 95 percent written by the time we got out of there and headed to the studio. With, of course, the notable exception of the song “Black Parade” itself, that has its own sort of strange and storied history.

It has been revealed that while they’re writing in the house, where are you and what are you doing?Every day, Monday through Friday, I’d show up with my engineer, Doug McKean, and I set up some fancy microphones in this giant, crazy living room that they had. The great room in that house looked like it was, like, 1,500 square feet. And we put the band in there with a PA, like a smaller PA, so that we could record whatever the band was writing and doing. So the writing was done almost live.

Gerard liked to just sing over the band. And someone would bring in a riff and we would just start jamming and recording. And the great news is that all of those recordings actually are now available online. I think there was a big box set of these live two-track recordings that are sort of the precursor — they’re the demos that we made the album from.

In a recent development, yeah, those are available to stream now.We put them on these DAT tapes. I had a special digital audio tape recorder, which was basically a tape that would be equivalent to CD quality. We would set about writing and creating and capturing these compositions, and working on the structure of them and what have you, so that we could then go into the studio, which is, of course, radically more expensive, and make the record.

Was Gerard having his night terrors at the house, and did he think they were caused by the house?You’d have to ask him if they were being caused by the house. But one thing for sure is the house had an effect on him, because it was a strangely haunted, dark place.

And he did talk about the night terrors, and he did talk about that he was going through a lot of things at that particular time. I think he was, like, a young man at the cusp at that time. I didn’t know where he was with his significant-other situation. There might have been something going on there. I don’t really know. But I would say this, I could tell he had a great record in him.

They’re a very emotional band, and they’re the nicest people. They’re very cordial to each other, and everything is on the up and up. But they also kinda would wear their hearts on their sleeves; if they were upset about something else in life, you could hear about it, you know? I was there to be very supportive. But the one thing for sure is that nothing ever got in the way of the music. We went to work. It was serious. We seriously worked 10, 12 hours a day.

When Mikey has to leave because it’s psychologically oppressive, does it make anyone else wonder, “Hey, maybe we should get the hell out of here too?”I think there was some conversation about it, but I also think, certainly, there were financial considerations. I think that there was a lease that we had to let expire, and, like, where were they gonna stay if they go, and what other money is that? ‘Cause we were responsible and [we were] on a budget.

It has been revealed that and you’re writing all this great stuff, so why not stay?That’s the other thing. The vibe in the daytime and into the evening, in terms of getting work done, it was working. You’re really correct on that.

In a recent development, so you go in the studio. Let’s talk about “Welcome to the Black Parade,” which started as “The Five of Us Are Dying.”So what was interesting is that it was a song that we thought was good, and we knew we were gonna put it on the record.

Recent findings suggest that but there [were] two things about it that kinda didn’t work. One was, I remember there was, “What’s the intro gonna be?” And “Do we just pop into the song?” And it never felt totally settled. And then the other thing was the chords on the chorus were… If you listen to “Five of Us Are Dying,” you’ll see that the chord structure was slightly different, and it didn’t feel like a hit record. It just felt like an OK song.

So what happened?I really gotta give credit to Gerard and the band. So I, for whatever reason, one day showed up to the studio early. And nobody was around, and we were at the Eldorado Studio in Burbank. And so I would sometimes sit there and just play the piano in the morning and just get my ears opened up and refreshed or whatever.

And lo and behold, Gerard shows up five minutes later. We were a good half an hour, 40 minutes before everybody. And so I’m just playing the piano, and he liked that ’cause I could play Queen songs and whatever. I remember him pointing at me once when we were up at the Paramour mansion, and I started playing things. He goes, “Oh, hey, listen to Cavallo. He can actually do shit on the piano. We should use that.”.

Recent findings suggest that so now here we are, like a month or two later, and we’re at Eldorado. And he goes to me, “Can you play…” And he cited the graduation theme, like “Pomp and Circumstance.” He goes, “But can you do that, but just make it go down?” And so I had one of those weird moments where I stated to myself, “Don’t think, just play.” And my fingers literally started playing, and Gerard almost immediately started singing, “When I was a young boy…” And it was really a magical thing, and we had a little voice note recorder or voice memo thingy, and we recorded it, and he goes, “OK, so this is the parade.” We were thinking of it as being, like, an interstitial moment in the record where you would hear a parade from half a mile away or a quarter mile away, and it’d start very light.

In a recent development, that’s why I played it with one finger at first. And then I started playing it with two hands, and then I started playing it as big as I could make it — loud. And then, now that the parade has passed you, it gets quieter again, right? So I worked it all the way back up to just the single-note thing, right? And the thing probably lasted two, two and a half minutes. And so then the idea was, OK, we’re gonna have marching bands, and we’re gonna have orchestral percussion and the horns and the whole thing.

But I went away with my family for a few days, and when I got back on Monday, Gerard states, “You gotta hear this. You gotta hear this.” And what they had done was they had taken the first half of “The Black Parade” and attached it to what would become the extended intro to [“The Five of Us Are Dying”]. And I was like, “Oh, my God, that totally works.”.

It has been revealed that what else did they change?I think Ray [Toro] or somebody fixed the chords on the chorus. The chorus became much more sing-along. And then all of a sudden that made sense. But what it really also did was, because we had a marching band and giant orchestrations in the intro, it afforded us the ability for me as a producer to say, “Now I can afford to have all these big orchestrations and all those things during the body of the song,” which normally you wouldn’t have a reason to do. It raised the bar of the song creatively to such a level that we could do something that in a weird way maybe on a pop-punk record had not been done before.

I remember I played it for one of my great mentors, Lenny Waronker, who was the longtime president of Warner’s, famous dude, and he went, “Holy shit. What the hell is that? I’ve never heard anything like that.” It actually worked, you know? So I remember thinking, “Wow, Lenny likes it. Yay.”.

Let’s talk about “Teenagers.”He really did mean what he was saying, but sometimes an artist can do what they would call a throwaway. Because he was concerned with — this is when Columbine happened, and kids were getting violent. And that song almost didn’t make the record.

What happened was there were some people that thought, “This is like an old-school rock & roll song.” And the argument was, “Why are we doing an old rock & roll song?” Like what they call a I-IV-V [chord-progression] song, like Chuck Berry. But what’s great about that is that my argument was, how do you write a contemporary I-IV-V song that is so great? And have the lyric be that meaningful? To me, that was the argument to do it. Right?

According to recent reports, it’s just an important record. And to be fair, it worked out, you know? Everybody agreed. It took a week or two. It was definitely a conversation, ’cause if you do listen to the record, I admit that it is an outlier on the album.

Industry observers note that but there was just something so compelling about that. At the beginning, it wasn’t obvious even how to cut it, but we did. I remember we all took turns at, “What should the bass be like?” You know? And I think Ray actually kinda figured it out. But anyway, the point is that the record came out and look what happened. It just exploded.

In a recent development, I believe it was your phone call that got Liza Minnelli on “Mama.”Yeah, so we were talking about, on “Mama,” who should play Mother War? The idea of this was like Mother War is this weird character. And there was a wonderful lady — Liz Rosenberg, Madonna’s publicist. And so I was kicking around Warner’s, like, does anybody know Liza Minnelli? I think it was Gerard’s idea. It was definitely the band’s idea. And I stated, “Let me see if I can get it.” So I called Liz Rosenberg and she said, “I can do it. I think I can get her.” And anyways, the fucking miracles, she did it. She got her.

Sources indicate that what was working with Liza like?One of the things that was so great about Liza is that she was so consummately professional that we got the takes that we wanted, and she was not done. She was like, “No, I need to keep doing this. Let me keep trying. Let me perfect this. Let me get this crying part down. Let me figure out how I can truly nail this performance.” And her attention to detail, I have to say, I was just so blown away by her.

It has been revealed that we haven’t necessarily had a ton of great guitar solo albums this century, but this is definitely one of them. Do any memories stand out?Both Ray and Frank [Iero] are great guitar players, and they did amazing things. But the thing that always stands out is the song “Dead!” And that first solo, because what’s crazy about that solo is that that happened by accident. It was supposed to just be the chords, and we weren’t gonna actually have a solo there. The chords were, like, enough.

Sources indicate that but Ray being as great guitar player as he is, I think we just hit record or whatever, and he had the guitar in his hand, and he just ripped that solo, actually just as like a warmup or something. And we went, “We gotta use it. We gotta use it,” and he was like, “No, no. We can’t use it. We can’t use that. That’s just…” And then we printed a rough mix of the whole thing and we kept living with it, and over the course of the next week or two, I was like, “Ray, we gotta use it. It’s too good.” And eventually he remarked, “OK, fuck, we’ll use the solo.” But what’s amazing is it highlights you how good a player he is, because that was something that was — how do I explain it? — an off-the-cuff, unplanned solo. How good is that? That this guy could just do that without even thinking about it.

The band hung out in a house for two months writing, and then recorded at a great studio. Would it be very difficult to get all that together in the current music industry, on a major label?Yes and no. It’s funny, if you look at the budgets back then for a band like that and the way the music business is now, it’s really comparing apples and oranges, right? I don’t think that Paramour was, like, that expensive, because if it’s 15 or 20 grand a month and you do it for two months, and you’re housing like five, six, seven guys, that’s actually cheap. And also rehearsing. That’s actually kinda inexpensive if you’re thinking about it in terms of real estate. If you were to pay a rehearsal place and hotels and all that kind of stuff, it’d be a lot more.

And then we went to Eldorado, which was not an A++ expensive three-grand-a-day place. It was actually more in the middle level. Like $1,200 or so — and I think we were able to crank that album out in, tops, two and a half months. So 10 weeks or something. That was a budget-conscious record, which made sense because they were a band on their way up. The prior record did well, but it wasn’t like there was like oodles of money running around all over the place.

According to recent reports, I was kinda known as a producer that could stay on budget. So we probably did this one in the $200,000 to $250,000 range, but that’s just a total fucking guess.

Was there any sense, working on Black Parade, that this was a band about to make just one more album and then not make one for a very long time?There was no indication during making Black Parade that it was gonna be only one more album, but there was indication near the end of Danger Days that there were feelings afoot, shall we say.

The band has stated there’s a new album coming. Are you working with them now?No, I was supposed to go see them at the Hollywood Bowl, and then I got the flu, so I didn’t go. But I’ve been in contact with Ray and Mikey. I really don’t know what their plans are. In a recent development, meanwhile, you have a hit record again, 20 years later. It just shows you the state of the music business being in such a weird place. But it’s also a good place. When I looked at it, just the idea that there’s a newly introduced piece of vinyl — I think when a band is really good and makes really good music and there’s also a bit of a scarcity about it, right? They haven’t made music in a long time. You put out this new piece of product and the hardcore fans will buy. I actually bought one myself the other day. I was at Amoeba and I said, “You know what? I should just buy one for good luck.”.

In a recent development, you pushed it over the top. It would’ve been Number Two if you didn’t jump in there.I bought a whole one copy at $40. It’s amazing, and they sold something like, I think, 70,000 of them or something. And I think that was just in the United States, unless that was worldwide, I don’t know. But I also know it was Number One in the U.K. But what’s interesting is those numbers are, in a weird way, like old-school, unheard-of numbers, because if you sell 70,000 at $40 list price, the gross is 2.8 million bucks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple only rolled out high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a new report offers an update on release timing.

A latest report from Kim Yeong-ho at ETNews provides a fresh enhancement on timing for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

Rumors have indicated for well over a year that Apple planned to push these models out of the typical fall launch window and introduce them in early 2027 instead.

Recent findings suggest that per ETNews, Samsung and LG are providing the display panels for the upcoming models, with Samsung the sole supplier for iPhone Air 2 and both companies splitting orders for iPhone 18. And their mass production plans signal a March release for the products.

Kim Yeong-ho, writing at ETNews:.

Samsung Display plans to begin mass production in January, while LG Display will start late this year…The Korean panel makers appear to be aligning their production plans with an expected March launch.

A March launch window lines up well with when Apple tends to ramp up product introductions following a slower winter. Earlier this year, iPhone 17e debuted in March alongside latest Macs and the iPad Air.

The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

Recent findings suggest that with Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the new models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

Breaking: iPhone Duo is getting three new features in iOS 27.3

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27.3 releases next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.
  • Apple is granting iPhone Duo consumers one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.
  • It has been revealed that face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient fresh option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 releases next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.

Apple is granting iPhone Duo consumers one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient fresh option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple:.

It has been revealed that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

Industry observers note that if your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most users, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

According to recent reports, on a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds upcoming face unlock feature for iPhone Duo.

Reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

You can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great latest option to have.

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces newly introduced iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use.

What should happen when you close your iPhone Duo’s folding screen? Apple has found that consumers have different preferences. Some want the iPhone to stay unlocked for continued use, while others prefer that it automatically locks when closed.

In iOS 27.3, Apple adds a upcoming setting so users can enable whichever behavior they prefer.

By default, iPhone Duo will work as it always has, staying unlocked after being closed. But inside Settings ⇾ Display & Brightness, iOS 27.3 provides the option of automatically locking upon being closed instead. You could achieve something similar before with Shortcuts, but now there’s a built-in setting too.

It’s not exactly a “upcoming feature,” but iPhone Duo consumers will also find that the system keyboard has changed in iOS 27.3. Apple tweaked the outer display keyboard to push keys closer together and make one-handed use easier.

Here’s a comparison of the old and new keyboards via Beta Profiles on X:.
