Breaking: Testing Terraform with AWS Emulator

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1335 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hatedabamboo

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, terraform initiative passes and demonstrates all green and all the necessary resource changes.
  • The problem with the difference between initiative and apply jobs is that plan can't possibly emulate every actual API call against a live infrastructure.
  • There are multiple tools that can emulate AWS services either partially or in full, but what they lack is the actual knowledge of the service architecture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, terraform initiative passes and demonstrates all green and all the necessary resource changes. You trigger apply and... the job fails with some obscure error that a resource can't be changed. You open another pull request and try again. And perhaps you encounter an error again. Sounds familiar? I bet it does. I encountered issues like this so many times I'm afraid to count. But recently AWS released a new tool called Emulator that emulates actual AWS API endpoints. And it should be great for tasks just like that!

The problem with the difference between initiative and apply jobs is that plan can't possibly emulate every actual API call against a live infrastructure. It's a safe assumption based on the static declarations we put into it – the order of application, the necessary parameters, the proper configuration values. These mock calls can't know for a fact that you already have a resource in AWS called "my-bucket-asdasdasd" or that you're trying to upgrade a PostgreSQL RDS instance from version 14 to version 18 without an explicit "apply immediately" flag. One may argue that one can always try to apply changes locally, but this kinda undermines the whole automation workflow. So what is the answer?

There are multiple tools that can emulate AWS services either partially or in full, but what they lack is the actual knowledge of the service architecture. It may be similar, but it won't be authentic, and sometimes this small difference may cause a lot of problems. After all, what can be the closest to an AWS API, if not the same AWS API, but ephemeral?

In a recent development, the benefit of the AWS Emulator is that it's a self-contained binary (or Docker container) that can be utilized locally or in a CI workflow. This means the usual "Initiative > Apply" terraform workflow changes to "Plan > Apply against mock AWS infrastructure to test the plan > Apply on actual AWS Infrastructure". This means slightly longer jobs, but if you're like me and apply jobs run on commits to the main branch after a PR, this saves you the hassle of creating a fresh branch just to fix the concern.

In a recent development, let's start with a local setup and see how we can utilize AWS Emulator with the actual Terraform code. All code is available in my example GitHub repository.

It has been revealed that first up, installation. You can either install aws-emulator via package manager, or build it with Docker. I'll use Docker to keep my system clear of yet another package:.

According to recent reports, and it's up and running! In the example above I set the container to live without limits (official AWS documentation proposes to set memory and swap limits: --memory=2g --memory-swap=2g, but for local that's fine). I also disabled authorization (flag -a off) to simplify things a bit.

To be sure aws-emulator is up and running, let's query the admin endpoint:.

Okay, fake AWS is live, let's deploy some infrastructure!

Recent findings suggest that I created an example AWS stack for Terraform and will use it in this article. First, let's configure Terraform to act against aws-emulator and not real AWS APIs. providers.tf will look like this:.

The difference between actual live infrastructure and a fake one is that we set up a bunch of flags to allow insecure connections (perhaps turning authentication off wasn't actually simpler?) and we set up an endpoint for each service we use in the setup to an emulator endpoint, which lives in the local Docker container:.

The rest of the configuration is as usual: resources, variables, modules (if any). Just what your project has.

In a recent development, let's proceed and test our setup. (I'll omit full terraform output otherwise this article would be 3 kilometers long).

According to recent reports, plan works! That's good to see, but not what we're here for. Still, a good sign. Now for the real test.

Sadly, the running aws-emulator container doesn't show in its logs which API requests it receives and what's happening under the hood, but I guess the tool is good enough as it is.

When you're done, stop the container:.

A container started with --rm removes itself after stopping, so no additional cleanup is needed. And as for the emulator -- it stores its state in memory, so each container restart drops all record of previous actions and any stale state.

Now for the real test: can we wrap the desired logic inside a CI pipeline? Let's think.

For successful invocation in the pipeline we will need almost everything the same, but we will be limited by time (the faster -- the better, and overall reasonable timeouts) and resources.

The workflow with terraform apply against aws-emulator is shown down below. For it I decided to try out package manager installation (builders are ephemeral anyway) and proper authentication. Full workflow with actual successful runs can be found in the example GitHub repository.

Sources indicate that this is a crude excerpt of the actual glorious workflow file that outlines the most crucial steps: emulator installation, terraform setup, strategy and apply. On the example terraform architecture the whole pipeline took 1m25s, which is okay in my opinion, but there is room for improvement: sprinkle some caching on top, leave validation, format check for local hooks, etc.

It's always nice when code someone wrote on the internet works from the start after you copy-paste it onto your machine. That's why I always run the described processes myself -- building, testing, fixing, retrying -- before publishing an article. But showing only the positive scenarios creates a false sense of trust in the tool.

Let's break something on purpose.

Industry observers note that in the example codebase I added a variable that, when enabled, makes the stack try to deploy a resource with an erroneous declaration. It will pass the plan job, but fail on apply.

According to recent reports, setting this variable to true at runtime will break our stack. Let's see:.

According to recent reports, and there we have it. The exact problem that arises only against actual API calls and not during a initiative job.

For scenarios exactly like this, the emulator is priceless.

Industry observers note that AWS Emulator is AWESOME. I'm rarely that excited about newly introduced tools lately (mostly because almost all of them are near/about AI), but this one is just so good and scratches that exact itch I felt for so long.

Industry observers note that for starters, it can't effectively emulate IAM policies and permission checks. This is a bummer, because permission validation is such a crucial step for production-ready security. Here's hoping that the tool will evolve further and it will be included in future updates.

Sources indicate that second, as a tool still a work-in-progress[1], its capabilities are quite limited. Even while writing the article I encountered several cases of 501 NotImplemented. It complicates things a bit if your infrastructure setup is huge and has a lot of quirks and weird configurations and super upcoming services. Still, AWS releases new versions quite often, and they're quite open about Emulator limitations, which is nice.

In a recent development, and last, but not least, is telemetry. AWS is explicit that it gathers telemetry and what this telemetry includes. This is honest behaviour and I like that approach. They even allow you to disable the telemetry, which further increases my trust in this tool. I understand the rationale behind this functionality (the tool is actively developed, they need the data to understand usage patterns and what goes wrong), but in the age of constant surveillance from Major Tech at every corner it still raises a slight concern. But then again, for the ultra-paranoid folks the code is open source and can be rebuilt with telemetry torn out of it.

Recent findings suggest that as of the moment of writing this article, AWS Emulator has been live for 1 day. ↩︎.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Expectations that a new Avengers: Doomsday teaser or trailer is imminent have hit fever pitch over the weekend following cast member Hayley Atwell’s omission while signing autographs in New York that it is dropping on Monday (November 23).

“There’s a new trailer dropping on Monday… am I allowed to have remarked that?” Atwell, who returns to the franchise as Peggy Carter, told fans on Friday night.

Industry observers note that disney has also revealed a sneak peek for November 30 during The Wonderful World of Disney: Holiday Spectacular on ABC, but this is believed to be a different tease. Related Stories News Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar's Film Committee News Egyptian Music Star Mohamed Mounir Gets Biopic - Doha Industry Days.

A few hours prior to Atwell’s omission, some 7,000 miles away in Qatar, co-director Joe Russo had also hinted at fresh drops before the picture’s opening by Disney on December 18, telling fans to keep checking their feeds. Watch on Deadline.

Talking in a fireside chat at the Qatar Film Committee’s second Doha Industry Days, Russo explained that the four teasers, preceding an official trailer this summer, had played an integral role in the final version of the film.

He remarked it had been a way to connect with the fans, which was essential because the audience landscape had changed so much since Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame in 2018 and 2019 respectively.

“I have to work extra hard to subvert your expectations and be aware of who you are as a viewer and how you’re changing,” said Russo.

“The last time I did this, in 2018, 2019, is very different than now because we’ve been through a pandemic; lots of people spent a lot of time on social media. Movies saw a tremendous downturn, streaming saw a tremendous upturn, and now that all seems to be reversing. So, it shifts constantly,” he said. “You have to be a futurist to try to predict where the market is going.”.

“I have to interact with the fans in order to understand what is moving them, what is working for them,” he noted. “What we’ve been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019.”.

“I had this idea, why don’t we start the story a year early? Why don’t we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie… we did four trailers that were sprinkled out,” he continued.

Kicking off on December 23, 2025, the first trailer showing Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) returning home, unpacking his Captain America suit, and holding a baby. A teaser on November 30 highlighted Thor (Chris Hemsworth) praying to Odin for strength. This was followed onJanuary 6 2026 drop featuring the X-Men and a January 13 teaser, featuring the Wakandans and Fantastic Four.

“We’ve done a series of tags around the characters because the story actually started in January of last year, and you’ve been watching it slowly unfold and these are all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18,” he mentioned.

In a recent development, “It’s slowly investing them [fans] emotionally. But I’m also getting feedback as that’s happening and we can make adjustments as we go, based on what people are tracking or not tracking,” he continued.

Industry observers note that “It’s a very complicated story also, so I have to make sure that they’re following each little crumb we give them. If they get the wrong thing from it, then I have to make adjustments, knowing that they might have the wrong idea about it.”.

Talking about his return to the Avengers franchise alongside brother Anthony Russo, Joe Russo said he had been reluctant at first because of the immense challenge of pulling off a Marvel movie at that scale.

He credited Robert Downey Jr., who played Tony Stark/Iron Man in Avengers: Endgame, with planting the seed for a return to the franchise, with his revelation that he was down to play Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom.

“He’s a very dear friend of mine, but I also think he’s the greatest actor of his generation. This is a supremely talented, charismatic human being. And he translates incredibly well on a global scale. There’s something about the nature of his performance that translates,” mentioned Russo.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s a style that belongs to these films that allows them to work in every market around the world. He just embodies that,” he remarked.

Russo stated Robert had gently enquired whether he was up for coming back to the Avengers franchise over dinner a couple of years ago.

Industry observers note that “I was still recovering from Infinity War and Endgame. And I was hesitant… he’s smart, he doesn’t push too much, he just kind of dropped the idea on the table and let it sit there, and then after dinner, he brought it up again, and I was like, ‘I don’t think I could do it, I’m still too tired.’ And then this festered for a little bit. And he didn’t even really tell me what he was going to do going back,” recall Russo.

It has been revealed that “And then another conversation happened where he mentioned, ‘You know, I’m going to play Doom’. And I said, ‘That’s a really clever idea”. I can see a corollary there. There are thematics, greatest hero, greatest villain. There’s a multiverse. There’s a reason for being. There’s a compelling idea there. And I went, ‘Well, of course, who else could play the greatest villain other than you.”.

Industry observers note that “It started to simmer in my brain a little bit. But we didn’t have a story. You can’t just show up with an empty canvas, so I still stated no.”.

Russo credited longtime collaborator, screenwriter Steve McFeely, with coming up with the premise that gave a way in to writing Doomsday, after they had been pitching ideas back and forth.

“Steve McFeely called me and said, ‘I have a crazy idea about how this works… what would happen if you left the cameras rolling at the end of Endgame? What’s the very next scene that happens,” recounted Russo.

“I said, “That’s really risky for a movie that had the level of success it did. You’re going to impact people’s emotional investment in it… this could blow up in your face,’ and then I went, ‘I love it’,” he continued.

“The concept was like that’s a very happy ending for one character. And what if happiness is finite, and what if you have to take happiness from someone else to create your own happiness… What happens in that story? That’s where I went, ‘Right, I know what to do with this.” The idea that like there was a cost to a happy ending.”.

50 Years Ago Today: The Beach Boys Play Pivotal ‘Brian’s Back’ Concert in Cincinnati

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band.
  • Just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence.
  • Industry observers note that the Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their upcoming work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band. “We’re thrilled to have him back.”.

Just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence. But the Beach Boys were the beneficiaries of an enormous nostalgia wave that swept America in the mid-1970s, giving us American Graffiti, Happy Days, Sha Na Na, and Grease.

Industry observers note that the Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their upcoming work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974. As a result, they dumped most of the recent material from their live repertoire and began playing arenas and even stadiums. “We knocked them dead every time we went out just playing the hits,” Al Jardine told Rolling Stone in 2025. “It allowed us to grow musically at home while we could continue to entertain. It was a nice balance.”.

But by 1976, as Endless Summer mania began petering out, the group needed a fresh gambit to keep drawing the substantial crowds. That’s why band manager Steve Love decided to rouse Brian Wilson from his bed and get him back on the road for the first time since 1964, generating a groundswell of interest in the band.

It has been revealed that they promoted the “Brian’s Back” campaign with an NBC television special put together by Lorne Michaels and the original Saturday Night Live team, which included a legendary sketch where Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi storm into Brian’s bedroom as the “Surf Police” and force him to surf for the first time. Annie Leibovitz shot a classic photo of Wilson standing on the sand that day in his blue robe, which appeared on the Nov. 4, 1976, cover of Rolling Stone.

Much of the press outside of Rolling Stone presented Wilson as a goofy eccentric rather than a genuine genius. “Brian is like an amiable child (violence was never one of his symptoms) trying to relearn the simple social graces,” People wrote. “As Brian told Mike [Love] lately, ‘I’m tired of being a failure.'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Sources indicate that that’s why he decided not only to join the tour but also to produce a upcoming Beach Boys record for the first time since Pet Sounds. The result was the underwhelming 15 Big Ones, which is thin on new originals and heavy on classic covers like Chuck Berry’s “Rock and Roll Music,” the Dixie Cups’ “Chapel of Love,” and Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill.”.

According to recent reports, brian Wilson was an infrequent presence throughout their highlights in the summer of 1976, but fully committed to a winter tour in November and December that followed a two-month hiatus from the road, giving him time to record The Beach Boys Love You. The run of dates began Nov. 22 at the Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati, Ohio. Tickets ($7.50 in advance and $8.50 on show day) were unreserved throughout the entire venue, which encouraged fans to line up all day to secure choice spots.

In a recent development, (Three years later, 11 Who fans were trampled to death when doors opened at this same venue. As a result, Cincinnati outlawed “festival seating” at concerts. The ban wouldn’t be lifted until 2002, when Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played an arena show at the U.S. Bank Arena on the Rising tour.).

In a recent development, the Beach Boys show opens with “Wouldn’t It Be Nice” and “Palisades Park,” before Mike Love welcomes “my cousin, the one and only, the magnificent, Brian Wilson!” The crowd roars as he briefly stands up from his perch behind the piano, and then they kick into “Little Deuce Coupe,” “Darlin’,” “In My Room,” and “God Only Knows” while the crowd squeals with delight. Related Content Al Jardine Writes Open Letter to Fellow Beach Boy Mike Love: 'Praying For Your Recovery' Watch John Stamos and the California Sound Substitute for an Ailing Mike Love at Epcot Center The Beach Boys Cancel Final 2026 Concert The Beach Boys Canceled Another Show. A John Stamos Spinoff Group Is Taking Their Spot.

According to recent reports, “Brian was introduced early on in the first set, and most of the crowd stood to acknowledge one of the giants in the history of rock,” noted a review by Dennis Freeman of the News Record. “He didn’t do much, sat impassively behind his piano, but it was crucial to the group that he was with them again.”.

According to recent reports, after warming the crowd up with oldies, they shifted the show to the present with Al Jardine’s “Back Home” from 15 Significant Ones. It goes over particularly well with this crowd since it’s all about going back to Jardine’s birthplace of Ohio. “Well, I’m going back this summer to Ohio,” he sings. “I’m going to seek out all my friends I’ve always known/I’m going back to that farm that I remember.” (The song fell out of the band’s rotation in 1978 and wasn’t brought back until a Jardine and the Pet Sounds Band concert in Warren, Ohio, earlier this year.).

“How would you like to hear a couple of upcoming ones we haven’t even done for the public yet?” Mike Love asks the crowd after “Back Home.” “These aren’t even released yet. They will be out in January on our new album. Keep it quiet and don’t go singing to too many groups since they might rip it off. The first one we’re going to do is called ‘Love Is a Woman.’ It sends chills up and down where I won’t tell you. The other one is a song about being on an airplane, so we call it ‘Airplane.’ So listen real good. We hope you like it.”.

It has been revealed that nobody in the arena had any idea they were witnessing a historic moment. This was the first time anyone outside the tight Beach Boys circle had heard even a note of music from The Beach Boys Love You. And even though many fans likely used this as an opportunity to run to the bathroom or grab a beer, the group did a magnificent job on both. “Airplane” is especially transcendent. (Sadly, they’d only play Love You songs a handful more times, and they wouldn’t go near any of it after 1979. It wasn’t until Al Jardine’s inaugural tour with the Pet Sounds Band in 2025 that Love You finally got the treatment it deserved in front of live audiences.).

They win the audience back with a trio of 1960s songs (“Catch a Wave,” “Heroes and Villains,” and “Surfin’ USA”) before introducing the crowd to a local woman named Joellyn Lambert, a former taxi driver who drove Jardine through town in 1970 and inspired his song “Susie Cincinnati.” They recorded it for 15 Substantial Ones and placed an ad in the local paper prior to the show seeking her out. “Attention!!!” reads the notice. “The Beach Boys are looking for the lady cab driver named Suzi who picked them up six years from the airport. Group wants the person to be guest at their November 22 concert at Riverfront Coliseum.”.

Lambert was stunned when the Cincinnati Post tracked her down and arranged the visit. “I still can’t believe this is really happening,” she told the paper. “I’m now stopped on the street and asked if I’m really ‘Susie Cincinnati.'”.

The deep cuts continued with “It’s Okay,” “A Casual Look,” “Feel Flows,” and “Everyone’s in Love With You” before they closed out the night with a long run of surf-era hits that finished with “Fun, Fun, Fun.”.

Industry observers note that “We danced, clapped and sang our way through classic after classic, each song bringing back memories of summers past,” wrote Freeman in the News Record. “‘Surfer Girl’ led into ‘California Girls’ and climaxed with ‘Good Vibrations.’ The audience was pretty young, mainly 18-year-olds, and it was fascinating to note the songs which were greeted with the most applause were the group’s early pre-Beatles hits.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It indicates the timelessness of the Beach Boys’ music,” he continued. “It also indicates that rock critics are wrong that time is up for the group. Even if the apparent re-emergence of the group as a creative force is short-lived, be assured the people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.”.

They would indeed. But what they didn’t want to hear or see was basically any song they recorded after “Do It Again.” Those fans were in luck since the Beach Boys essentially abandoned any pretense that they were anything but a perpetual-motion 1960s jukebox not long after the 1976 Brian’s Back tour. The idea of seven songs from a new album and another two from an album that wasn’t even released yet, as they did in Cincinnati, soon became unthinkable. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

Sources indicate that the Beach Boys returned to Cincinnati on Oct. 10 of this year for a show at the PNC Pavilion at Riverbend. Love is now the final legit member in the touring lineup, and this was a deeply upsetting concert for many fans since it was the first one where he was unable to stand or even sing. He’s been battling a severe health ailment for at least the past year and hasn’t been seen since a show the following night in Nashville.

Industry observers note that whatever happens going forward, the News Record was prophetic back in 1976 when it mentioned “people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.” Does that mean they’ll become a zombie group like Foreigner or the Four Tops that continues to tour without any original members? Could Jardine finally be given the chance to front his own version of the Beach Boys? Are their children going to take over? There’s simply no way to know at this point. But it’s very hard to imagine a summer passing without some version of the Beach Boys on the road.

Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That remarked, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

According to recent reports, “I’ve always joked that I’m a little bit Jew-ish-ish with a big hyphen,” claims Culture Club frontman Boy George. George’s arrival is a rare one, as most Western artists have steered clear of the country, which has been plagued by political infighting, wars in Gaza and Iran, and global criticism for its handling of the conflicts.

But the 65-year-old is defying convention with characteristic flair. George burst on the pop scene in 1982, one of the first MTV stars with the New Wave hit “Do You Really Want to Hurt Me?” Challenging gender and cultural norms in an oversize hat, Rasta dreads, drag makeup, and a T-shirt that spelled Culture Club in Hebrew (Havurat Aguda), Boy George was an instant sensation and ruled the pop charts for years to come.

According to recent reports, four decades later, Boy George is still advocating for multiculturalism and LGBTQ+ rights, but his hometown of London feels less tolerant. On his way to the doctor in April, he arrived at the Jewish neighborhood of Golder’s Green moments in the wake of an antisemitic stabbing spree, the culmination of a disturbing 82 percent uptick in physical assaults in the U.K. in the first half of 2026, per the Community Security Trust. He then visited the Nova exhibit in London and released the reggae-infused single “We Will Dance Again” (Od Nirkod in Hebrew) in late July on Instagram and X. He made his position clear through the lyrics: “You say genocide/I say war…. You condemn the Jews with selective memory/Musicians holding flags, mouthing like sheep…. You never mention Oct. 7/Young girls raped against trees, murdered brutally/For the crime of dancing.”.

It has been revealed that the song prompted a swift and harsh backlash. He said he “parted ways” with longtime manager of his BGP label, Tony Pontius, was removed from Bandcamp for using AI on the track, lost old friends like Human League and Heaven 17 founder Martyn Ware, was disinvited from a memorial honoring stylist friend Pam Hogg, and was pulled from a West End revival of “Jesus Christ Superstar.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, never one to back down, George spoke out, released his single with live instrumentation on Warner Music/ADA in October (it charted in the U.K., France, Greece, and Latvia), and announced he would perform in Israel, boycotts be damned. While there, he met with Oct. 7 survivors, victims’ families and held a press conference at the site of the Nova Festival in Re’im, where Hamas killed 378 concertgoers and staff, took 44 hostages, and sexually assaulted concertgoers, according to an independent U.N. investigation.

Upon his return to London, George reflected on his trip, the blowback he received, and the alarming rise in antisemitism in an interview with Rolling Stone.

It has been revealed that is it true that “We Will Dance Again” was inspired by your visit to the Nova Exhibition in London?Well, it started before that. A lot of musicians were putting flags onstage and using words that I didn’t necessarily support. I had posted a few positive comments online [supporting Nova survivors], and a couple of artists did the usual “shame on you, shame on you.” And I started to see it was getting a lot of rage online. I [thought], I’ll write about what’s going on, because there’s only so many love songs you can write. I’ve known Jewish people since I was a teenager in London. Being in the fashion world and obviously rock ‘n’ roll, it would be very amazing if you didn’t know someone Jewish.

Sources indicate that given that, were you surprised by the lack of compassion for Oct. 7 victims?I think people were very quick to celebrate what happened on October the 7th and change the narrative, twist it around, make it about something else. And it felt that some of the reaction was already planned. As soon as I saw a Palestinian umbrella, I was like, they got products. This isn’t just people with cardboard and some words scratched on it. A lot of musicians I respected were saying ‘Free Palestine.’ And there was no voice for the Jewish community in London. I went to New York and was given an award by [ewish publication] Tablet magazine for my support of the Jewish people, and I felt a little bit like a fraud. But at that point, nobody was saying anything. So I was kind of like a lone wolf in that sense. Being an ally can be fraught these days…Sometimes you need allies from outside, like straight guys supporting gay people and trans people. You need allies that are not part of that group. In the Seventies, when we started Culture Club, our whole ethos was about anti-racism and anti-prejudice. All that stuff was really the backbone of what we were singing about, which is why we called ourselves Culture Club, and why we wore the Jewish star and presented Rastafarian images. We probably naively were mixing up a lot of religious ideas, but it was more about that feeling of why can’t people just live in harmony? … My tastes are very eclectic, not only musically but also culturally. As a kid, if I saw a religious Jewish guy, I’d be like, “That look!” I am interested in other people and human beings.

Sources indicate that so, was your iconic hat a nod to the Hasidic look?That hat was an original Hasidic hat, and in fact, when John [Moss, Culture Club drummer and George’s former boyfriend] went to buy it, because my initials are G.O.D., for George O’Dowd, they wouldn’t put that in the hat. It would have been great!

Recent findings suggest that what’s it like performing your old hits now?I feel like it’s an ending of something for me. I’m not saying I’ll never sing those songs again. Of course I will, but my feeling is that next year I might start a very different type of band, a punk band or a reggae band. I just need to do something different, because I feel like that old boy George doesn’t really exist anymore.

I’d grown up in a very dysfunctional family, where there was a lot of fighting, and you grow up thinking that that’s normal. I went from one dysfunctional relationship to another, which is why I joke now that creativity is my lover. One thing I’ve learned in the last 10, 15 years is that songwriting is not hard. Finding what you want to say is the biggest challenge. A song like “We Will Dance Again” kind of wrote itself. When I was at Nova, I saw “we will dance again” written everywhere, and I was like, well, there’s the hook! And then the rest of it was simply looking at what was being noted and using those words in a very blatant way, literally reading stuff out of the newspaper and challenging that as a writer, which I think is the job of an artist to say, “Is there another way of looking at this?” I’ve never said anything negative about Palestine, or anywhere else. It’s about me saying, “I know my Jewish friends are good people. I know this to be a fact.” They fed me more than any other race. You want to be my friend? Feed me.

So touring Israel was less of a political stance than a humanitarian one for you?I don’t really have a stance. I don’t even know what that means. I’ve been called everything you can think of: Goy George, Genocide George, all of that stuff. I felt like I had to go, and now that I’m back in London, it was the right thing to do. I will go back and do a recording of the songs that I did at Menorah [Mivtachim Arena], because it would be great to put it out as a Boy George in Israel tribute. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

In a recent development, “I’m eager not to continue purposely doing Robert Eggers’ House of Horror,” Eggers mentioned during a recent Q&A. “I don’t need to do the Mummy or The Opera. Not to say that I won’t, but I think I need a break.”.

In a recent development, eggers’ comments come amid recent talks with Focus Features over an adaptation of William Shakespeare’s Romeo & Juliet, which he explained would be “a break” from the next horror pic he was planning. Watch on Deadline.

Sources indicate that “I was doing something else,” noted Eggers. “But what happened was, after Werwulf, I was writing another horror movie, and it got so dark again, and I was like, ‘I need a break. So, I’ll do something about two teenagers killing themselves.'”.

In a recent development, following his 2015 feature debut The Witch, Eggers has been praised as a upcoming master of horror with films like The Lighthouse (2019), Nosferatu (2024) and Werwulf, premiering Dec. 25 from Focus Features.

In Werwulf, a man (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) in 14th century England finds him and his family threatened by a ravenous beast haunting the town. The film also stars Lily-Rose Depp, Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson and more.

According to recent reports, the Prison Service of England and Wales requested that the Google-owned YouTube take down the video, saying Brand’s message was “distressing for victims.” However, Google denied the request, stating that — while hurtful for the victims — Brand’s video didn’t violate any of the platform’s rules. Breaking: The Transvoxel Algorithm

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Transvoxel

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Transvoxel Algorithm is a method for seamlessly stitching together neighboring triangle meshes generated from voxel data at differing resolutions so that level of detail (LOD) can be used with large voxel-based datasets such as volumetric terrain in next-generation video games.
  • Recent findings suggest that voxel-based terrain systems are increasing in popularity because they remove the topographical limitations of conventional elevation-based terrain systems and provide the ability to create more complex structures like caves, overhangs, and arches.
  • Triangle meshes for adjacent voxel terrain blocks are rendered at two different resolutions near a cave entrance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Transvoxel Algorithm is a method for seamlessly stitching together neighboring triangle meshes generated from voxel data at differing resolutions so that level of detail (LOD) can be used with large voxel-based datasets such as volumetric terrain in next-generation video games. The algorithm was invented by Eric Lengyel in 2009 and implemented in the C4 Engine. This web page provides a high-level overview of the Transvoxel Algorithm, links to additional information, and data tables that can assist in an implementation.

Recent findings suggest that voxel-based terrain systems are increasing in popularity because they remove the topographical limitations of conventional elevation-based terrain systems and provide the ability to create more complex structures like caves, overhangs, and arches. Triangle meshes are typically generated from voxel data using the Marching Cubes algorithm, and the larger numbers of triangles that it generates makes a level-of-detail (LOD) system even more notable for high-performance rendering of large terrains. A natural way to implement level of detail for voxel-based terrain is to simply triangulate the voxel data at multiple resolutions, but this leads to the well-known problem of cracks forming along the boundary between meshes representing different resolutions, as shown in Figure 1. While it is relatively simple to patch these types of cracks in a robust manner for elevation-based terrain, the topographical freedom allowed by voxel-based terrain makes the patching process vastly more difficult because the structure of edge mismatches on the boundary plane can be much more complex. The Transvoxel Algorithm introduces the concept of a “transition cell” to smoothly and seamlessly connect voxel terrain meshes across multiresolution boundaries. The algorithm is designed so that only local voxel data is required for each transition cell, and this allows fast retriangulation in cases where the voxel data is dynamically changing in a real-time application.

In a recent development, figure 1. Triangle meshes for adjacent voxel terrain blocks are rendered at two different resolutions near a cave entrance. (a) Cracks are visible along the boundary between the blocks, allowing the sky in the background to show through, and a large hole appears where the terrain surface is nearly tangent to the boundary plane between the blocks. (b) A wireframe is overlaid to show the triangles generated by Marching Cubes. (c) The surfaces of differing resolutions are seamlessly joined by triangles generated for transition cells using the Transvoxel Algorithm, which follows in the footsteps of Marching Cubes but operates on an alternate arrangement of voxels at the boundary between cells of different resolutions. (d) The wireframe overlay reveals the triangles corresponding to the transition cells.

The Transvoxel Algorithm works by inserting special transition cells in between regular cells along the boundary between voxel data sampled at one resolution and voxel data sampled at exactly half that resolution. Instead of considering all possible combinations of voxel state for both the full-resolution and half-resolution data at a transition boundary, which would require that approximately 1.2 million cases be handled, we consider only nine samples of the high-resolution data. This gives us a much more manageable 512 cases to handle, and these cases happen to fall into the 73 equivalence classes shown in Figure 2. Every transition cell is filled with one of these triangle patterns in order to perfectly fill the seams, cracks, and holes that appear between meshes of different resolutions, as was done for the cave in Figure 1.

Sources indicate that in Figure 2, black dots represent voxels that lie inside solid space, and corners without a dot represent voxels that lie outside in empty space. Green triangles are front-facing polygons, and red triangles are back-facing polygons.

Get print version (18 × 24 inch wall poster).

Figure 2. These are the 73 equivalence classes into which the 512 possible transition cell cases fall.

Like the Marching Cubes algorithm, the Transvoxel Algorithm is efficiently implemented using a set of look-up tables that provide information about each of the 512 possible cases that can arise. These tables are not easy to generate, so I am providing the tables that I made in the following repository. There are comments in the .cpp file that describe what the numbers mean.

Transvoxel data tables on GitHub.

Eric Lengyel’s Dissertation, University of California at Davis, 2010. This dissertation goes into great detail about the Transvoxel Algorithm and multiresolution voxel terrain in general. It also describes how the algorithm can be efficiently implemented.

Industry observers note that lengyel, Eric. “Transition Cells for Dynamic Multiresolution Marching Cubes”. Journal of Graphics, GPU, and Game Tools. Vol. 15, No. 2 (2010), A K Peters. DOI: 10.1080/2151237X.2011.563682.

A complete implementation of the Transvoxel Algorithm is included with the C4 Engine.

In a recent development, lengyel, Eric. “Voxel-Based Terrain for Real-Time Virtual Simulations”. PhD diss., University of California at Davis, 2010.

In a recent development, it’s been about a year and a half since rapper and streamer PlaqueboyMax first spoke to Rolling Stone. In that time, the music industry has caught up with the popularity of streamers, as a growing set of major names — from Drake to Mariah Carey — have dabbled in the format. For Max, who has spent years making music in front of viewers, that means being something of an established figure in an evolving rap landscape.

“It’s been crazy,” he notes. “I’m really passionate about music, and I’m just happy that I’m able to merge my worlds and my passions together to make it one major world.”.

Industry observers note that max’s recent “Rising Star” competition, something like Star Search or American Idol for the underground rap generation, brought together six rappers with growing fanbases on one livestream where they’d create music and eventually perform for a real audience. The contest has its origins in two of Max’s streaming formats. “In the Booth,” which he started in 2024, lets viewers watch music being made. He was also doing “Song Wars” around then, putting songs up for an audience’s judgment. As he kept doing those streams, he wanted to spend more time with the artists. What else would people want to know about somebody they’d just watched make a song?

It has been revealed that “These are concepts where people are making songs and fresh art is being created live,” he says. “It’s very fascinating. And ‘Rising Star’ is basically a byproduct of these things, but taken even further.”.

The weekend format lets the audience spend hours with the contestants, who have personalities and frustrations to contend with as they’re making music. Max would like some of that audience to stick with them afterward.

“My whole premise with ‘Rising Star’ is that I want to find artists of the next generation that are coming up now, as opposed to maybe an already established artist and allow them to showcase what they’re doing and what they’re capable of and who they are as artists through this event.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

According to recent reports, he recruited Lil Yachty, with his years of experience making records and maintaining a career, alongside creators Cuffem and Funny Marco. Music advice from the rapper, entertainment from the creators: Max wanted both on the panel, with enough to keep his viewers watching.

“So I would say picking judges came down [to] just me picking people I appreciate, who I mess with, and just bringing them into my world and making it all one amazing product,” he states.

Industry observers note that yachty had plenty to say. Max remembers him taking five minutes to get into an individual artist’s work, which could make for an uncomfortable critique.

“Some of them were getting grilled, but it’s just like he’s giving them real feedback that if they listen, it will help them as an artist, and I love that,” Max says. “That’s what the purpose was.”.

Getting grilled in public can’t be much fun. I ask Max if anybody went away upset about it. Some artists were frustrated with the criticism, he says, or with their placement in the fan vote, but he stops short of calling them offended.

“They were frustrated either with their placements or I’d say sometimes the feedback they were getting, but I wouldn’t say that any artist that was competing took it the wrong way,” he states. “They were definitely just working hard and just passionate and hungry.”.

It has been revealed that but the thing Max remembers most is the show at the Belasco that closed the weekend. He’d spent all that time watching the artists work, and then got to watch them perform. Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.

This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.

Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:.

I hit my Siri AI usage limit, it still works though, including complex questions pic.twitter.com/XYYNPMnSnn.

In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.

Industry observers note that one question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:.

Suppose it gets it wrong like it does most of the time. I wonder if that still counts.

Industry observers note that but leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”.

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”.

Sources indicate that it would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the tech giant.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly 20 years later, Danny Ocean is trying to get the gang back together for Ocean’s 14, which was expected to begin filming in 2026.

David Leitch, who is attached to direct the fourth installment in the heist film franchise, recently noted that George Clooney and his Smokehouse producing partner Grant Heslov have delivered a “great script,” but scheduling challenges stand in the way.

It has been revealed that “Oh, I mean, there’s a great script and I think everybody’s excited about moving it forward,” he told People. “I think it’s always been about getting all those people together, and their schedules are always the issue.”.

Leitch added, “Look, there’s a lot of excitement around it and … George and Grant did incredible work on the script. So, yeah, a lot of motivation to make it happen.” Watch on Deadline.

Clooney starred as Danny Ocean in the 2001 Steven Soderbergh-helmed remake of the 1960 Rat Pack film, reprising the role in Ocean’s Twelve (2004) and Ocean’s Thirteen (2007).

In January 2025, Leitch was in early talks to direct the next installment. Last October, the 2x Oscar winner Warner Bros. approved the budget for Ocean’s 14, which he expected to begin filming this year.

Ocean’s 14 will mark the first installment in the main franchise not directed by Soderbergh, after Gary Ross helmed the 2018 female-led spin-off Ocean’s 8, starring Sandra Bullock as Danny’s sister Debbie Ocean.

Meanwhile, Bradley Cooper is attached direct an Ocean’s 11 prequel, which will star himself and Margot Robbie as Danny Ocean’s parents.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As John Madden‘s life gets the biopic treatment, his longtime colleague and friend Al Davis‘ family is not pleased with their late patriarch’s portrayal.

It has been revealed that las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis, whose father Al recruited Madden to coach for the NFL team when they were located in Oakland in 1967, criticized David O. Russell‘s Madden for its “totally unfair” depiction his father (portrayed by Christian Bale), who died at age 82 in 2011.

“It was full of turducken,” he told USA Today of the movie, referencing the Thanksgiving dish Madden popularized.

Industry observers note that mark continued, “As far as representations of my dad, yeah, that hurts, and I did the best I could to protect him. It’s absolutely a crime that they’re able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there’s nobody around to protect their legacies. It’s just unfair. I don’t know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest.” Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that he doesn’t consider his father “a pimp like Christian Bale played him, but that’s fine,” noting, “And I don’t blame Christian Bale. I don’t blame Nicolas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do.”.

Having screened the film two weeks before its release, Mark was surprised by a scene depicting the 1978 preseason game that paralyzed Latest England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley, in which Al discourages Madden (Nicolas Cage) from seeing the player in the hospital.

In a recent development, “One of the main legacies of my father was how much he took care of people, whether it was on the Raiders or other teams,” noted Mark. “People that were ill or needed help or whatever. He helped so many players on other teams that it’s incredible. And he did it quietly.

Industry observers note that “And for them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John out of going to see him – that was just such a hurt to me personally, because that’s my father’s legacy, is how he treated people. No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That’s one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way,” added Mark.

While he said that scene “hurt” him, Mark added, “All the other crap, I could take all that (stuff). I don’t care if they talk about my haircuts and stuff like that. I don’t know what it had to do with anything, but I don’t mind that. They can do that to me. But to do that to somebody that’s passed away, that can’t defend himself, is totally unfair. And I’m sure that there’s gonna be thousands of people that could contradict what that clip portrayed my father as.”.

Recent findings suggest that mark added that the portrayal of his mother Carol Davis (played by Sienna Miller) and John’s wife Virginia Madden (Kathryn Hahn) is “all made up stuff too,” conceding, “But there are some, you know, elements of them in that. I will say that, but not much.”.

Co-written by Russell and Cambron Clark, Madden charts John Madden’s career from Raiders coach to TV broadcaster to the namesake of the Madden NFL video game franchise.

#119864. This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (897 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (897 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • Recent findings suggest that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • According to recent reports, to buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first announced. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

Recent findings suggest that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

According to recent reports, to buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

The simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you stated) to your “Notes to self” note.

To take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

It has been revealed that all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

It has been revealed that it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

There’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can initiative them better next time.

Sources indicate that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

But this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

It has been revealed that the Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

It has been revealed that I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I said it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

  • Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • It has been revealed that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • Website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something new. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

It has been revealed that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

Website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

Sources indicate that to make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

Recent findings suggest that with a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but says you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Recent findings suggest that here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

The finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a latest window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

Everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

Industry observers note that for something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

It has been revealed that I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a big family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a fresh website.

According to recent reports, bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Todd Boehly gave an insight into his no nonsense approach to investing in sports and entertainment in the concluding fireside chat of the Qatar Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days over the weekend.

The billionaire investor’s holding tech giant Eldridge holds some $75B in assets including stakes in Backrooms distributor A24, and Fulwell Entertainment as well as the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Sparks, the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Trent Rockets among many more.

In a recent development, the holding is also a partner with Deadline owner Penske Media in the Penske Media Eldridge unit encompassing live TV entertainment specialist Dick Clark Productions as well as events such as the Golden Globes and SXSW. Related Stories News Joe Russo Talks 'Doomsday' Teaser-Trailer Strategy Ahead Of Rumored Monday Drop: "I Have To interact With Fans" News Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar's Film Committee.

Industry observers note that boehly first connected with A24 cofounder Daniel Katz, when the latter headed Guggenheim Partners’ film finance group in New York, while he was president of the global investment firm before leaving to create Eldridge. Watch on Deadline.

“One of the things I believe is that there’s very few entertainment people that understand math… the math of entertainment is really about understanding how are you taking risk and then how are you distributing risk,” he noted in the chat entitled “Playing to Win”.

“It’s no different than any other industry, if you’re thinking about what amount of risk you are willing to take and then how are you going to feed that risk,” he added.

Boehly stated Katz had impressed him from the start for his ability to identify and work with risk during his time with Guggenheim Partners.

“Daniel’s real magic, when he worked on our trading floor from, let’s call it like 2008 to 2012, he didn’t take a lot of risks, but he said ‘no’ a lot,” he said.

In a recent development, “There was a slate that was done by a group called Stark Investments, and one of their massive films was Poseidon. I remember it demonstrated up on our desk. And Daniel was immediately like, this is a disaster. It’s going to cost so much money, you know, they’re not going to be able to make any return on it.”.

The $160M disaster movie by Wolfgang Petersen went down in film financing folklore after it faltered at the box office and failed to gross enough to cover its P&A costs.

Industry observers note that boehly provided $19M in seed money for A24 as Katz launched the company in 2012 with David Fenkel and Joh Hodges. It was last publicly valued at $3.5 billion in June 2024.

Industry observers note that “Everyone told me in Hollywood that there’s no room for another distribution company,” recalled the businessman. “His early successes with Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring were really structured finance trades.”.

“You’re not really allowed to talk about that in the entertainment world because everything’s creative and creator driven… what Daniel was really good at, because he sat on a trading desk and he understood risk and he understood math, he was really good at figuring out how am I going to get my money back using different windows.”.

Starring James Franco, Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers premiered in competition in Venice and went on to gross $31M.

“Spring Breakers cost a couple million bucks to buy, and he ended up making 10 million bucks or so very quickly on, because he really understood that it’s a structured finance straight,” stated Boehly.

He added that beyond Katz’s business savviness, the tech giant had also understood how to tap into social media to generate audience engagement as well as how to plug into trends of the moment.

“One of the things that A24 has done an amazing job at is being able to read the cultural zeitgeist. I think Civil War was really well timed; Marty Supreme was very well timed with Timothée Chalamet and his ascension as probably one of the top actors for the next couple of decades.”.

Boehly also highlighted A24’s strategy of growing a cohort of directors and actors, who returned to work with the company on a regular basis.

“He wants repeat customers. He wants the directors coming back… he wants the actors coming back… because then it’s not a transaction, it becomes a recurring business with enterprise,” remarked Boehly.

Recent findings suggest that “So many people think about the film business, ‘Oh, it’s a transaction’. But if you’re really thinking about how to build an enterprise, then you need to make sure that you have a recurring revenue base. And the way you do that in this industry is you get repeat users.”.

He also gave insight into how Katz constructs A24’s slate in a way that enables it to work with established names and newcomers and turn a profit, suggesting that over a portfolio of 15 films, nine would be “the core bread and butter”.

Sources indicate that “It’s a budget of 25 to 40 million bucks. It’s the expectation that he’s going to make 1.35 times,” he explained. “And if you think about the math of it again, you get 0.8 times your money back right away or very quickly. So, when you think about the risk that you have, you’re in for 0.2. If you make 1.35 and your risk capital is 0.2, but you’re going to make six, seven times that 0.2.”.

“And then he’ll take three substantial swings and make something that has the capacity to become multiple films out of the content… he’ll take 1.2 times. So, he’ll modify his expectations on the rate of return to achieve something that might have more enterprise value or longevity on the back of it.”.

Boehly suggested the final three films would be by up-and-coming young directors, and would require time, energy and effort rather than significant financial investments and risk.

“He’s always thinking about how do I build that portfolio in order to have my bread and butter, have the opportunity to have something that’s got longevity and then find someone who’s going to be special in the industry,” he noted.

💡 Key Takeaways
