📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully rolled out on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

According to recent reports, “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

It has been revealed that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

According to recent reports, more than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to proposal, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” notes Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

In a recent development, the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

According to recent reports, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu notes, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It has been revealed that it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

According to recent reports, “It will bounce probably several times,” indicates Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Recent findings suggest that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she indicates. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday indicates Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Industry observers note that idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

In a recent development, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel states the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

Industry observers note that the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Sources indicate that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Recent findings suggest that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

Sources indicate that the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

It has been revealed that one of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

According to recent reports, that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

It has been revealed that during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

According to recent reports, once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

Industry observers note that “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Recent findings suggest that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu states. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Prime Video just added a seriously bonkers survival movie that didn’t get enough attention — and it’s the most fun you’ll have streaming this weekend

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 2026 has been a pretty decent year for upcoming movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar.
  • It has been revealed that thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience.
  • In fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

2026 has been a pretty decent year for upcoming movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar. One such film is “They Will Kill You,” a gloriously bonkers mash-up of survival, comedy and horror that pits a tough-as-nails woman against a group of seriously unhinged cult members. The whole thing feels like a fever dream, with outrageous violence, ridiculous twists and enough carnage to keep you wondering what on earth you’re watching.

It has been revealed that thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience. Its theatrical run certainly didn’t do it any favors, with the movie reportedly earning approximately $19 million worldwide against a production budget of $20 million, making it a box office disappointment. That’s a shame, because while it’s not a perfect film by any means, it’s certainly not a bad one.

In fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far. It knows exactly how ridiculous it wants to be and has plenty of fun with its increasingly chaotic set pieces. I left the theater genuinely shocked by some of the things I witnessed, but also grinning at just how much fun I'd had. If you missed it on the massive screen, its arrival on Prime Video is a pretty good excuse to put that right, and here’s why.

According to recent reports, “They Will Kill You” follows Asia Reaves (Zazie Beetz), a young woman who takes a live-in housekeeping job at The Virgil, a luxurious Fresh York City apartment building, hoping to find her missing younger sister, Maria (Myha'la). However, Asia soon discovers that the building’s wealthy residents are hiding a terrifying secret: they’re members of a satanic cult that has been sacrificing unsuspecting workers for decades.

Recent findings suggest that when the residents attempt to make Asia their latest victim, they swiftly discover she’s not quite as helpless as they expected. Trapped inside the building with seemingly no way out, Asia must fight her way through its corridors and take on an increasingly dangerous group of attackers. With time running out and Maria caught up in the cult’s plans, Asia faces a brutal fight to get them both out alive.

I’ll admit, I was a little worried “They Will Kill You” might struggle to stand out, especially arriving shortly after “Ready or Not 2,” which has a pretty similar premise involving two sisters trying to escape a cult. Thankfully, Zazie Beetz gives this film a flavor of its own. She’s an absolute badass, throwing herself into some wonderfully chaotic fight scenes and getting covered in blood more times than I can count. There’s also a noticeably angrier edge to this movie, which I really appreciated. It’s a welcome addition to the horror-comedy genre that isn’t afraid to get properly nasty.

Sources indicate that storytelling isn’t exactly the film’s strong suit, and I wouldn’t say it does anything particularly compelling with its characters or central plot. But that’s not really why I’d recommend it. The real draw is the action, inventive kill scenes and completely unhinged body horror. There are also some wonderfully ridiculous twists involving the cult that had me laughing, while the final act goes so completely off the rails that I was practically squealing (little hint there). It’s an absolute hoot, and I had a ridiculous amount of fun watching it.

I also really enjoyed the film’s visual style. Director Kirill Sokolov uses graphic compositions that sometimes resemble comic-book panels, alongside unusual framing and some wonderfully eccentric camera angles. There are moments when the whole thing almost feels like you’re watching a video game, particularly during its more elaborate fight sequences. Yes, it’s a little unconventional, but I thought it worked brilliantly with the film’s exaggerated violence and chaotic energy. It gives “They Will Kill You” a distinct visual identity that helps it stand apart from other horror-comedies.

Industry observers note that there’s definitely a lack of genuine character connection here, largely because the story doesn’t give you much to work with, but Beetz is such a compelling screen presence that you naturally find yourself rooting for her anyway. She’s more than capable of carrying the film, and I’d happily watch her take on another ridiculous survival scenario. I also think “They Will Kill You” has some serious cult classic potential. It might not have found its audience at the box office back in March, but I wouldn't be surprised if it earns a lot more love in the years ahead as more people discover it. Sometimes all a film needs is a second chance, and this one certainly deserves it.

Stream "They Will Kill You" on Prime Video now.

Alix is a Senior Streaming Writer at Tom’s Guide, which basically means watching the best movies and TV shows and then writing about them. It’s a dream job for someone who’s been obsessed with storytelling since she first figured out how to work a remote.

Before joining Tom’s Guide, Alix honed her skills as a staff writer with outlets like Screen Rant and Bough Digital, where she discovered her love for the entertainment industry.

She heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is upgrading the Gemini app on Mac with computer use capabilities that can work across local desktop applications and the web.

The existing Task (previously Gemini Spark) functionality in the Mac app could just access local files in conjunction with Connected Apps, like @Gmail or @Google Calendar.

Computer use lets Gemini for Mac click and type on your behalf to accomplish multi-step tasks in local desktop apps and the web, like navigating menus and filling out forms.

Gemini works in an “isolated background window with a live preview right in your chat,” while your main screen and cursor remain free to use. On the safety front, you can stop Gemini at any time with one click, while you choose what apps Gemini uses. Google will pause for logins and payments, with confirmation needed for sensitive actions.

Industry observers note that many everyday tasks span desktop apps and websites that don’t connect to each other. Computer use handles the tedious steps in the background so you can save time without giving up your screen or cursor.

To use, add @Computer use to your prompt. In Customize > Connectors, you’ll see upcoming “Desktop” apps like Blender and Autodesk Fusion join the existing Git and Obsidian integrations.

FTC: We use income earning auto affiliate links. More.

Having a knee or hip replacement? A physical therapist explains prehab and the 4 moves to do before surgery

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you’re scheduled for an upcoming hip or knee replacement surgery, you’re far from alone.
  • According to recent reports, the good news?
  • “Surgery addresses the damaged joint, but patients still need strength to regain mobility and participate in rehabilitation afterward,” indicates Kaylee LeCavalier, PT, DPT, SCS, CSCS, CAPS, a physical therapist and board-certified sports specialist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you’re scheduled for an upcoming hip or knee replacement surgery, you’re far from alone. The American Joint Replacement Registry, managed by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, has surpassed 4.3 million hip and knee replacement procedures in its database. People heading into these operations have often spent months or years modifying how they move because of hip or knee pain, which can leave the muscles around the joints weaker than they should be.

According to recent reports, the good news? Prehab—a structured strengthening program you do before surgery—can help strengthen your knee and hip joints. A 2026 systematic review found early benefits for pain management, mobility, and functionality in people who underwent knee replacement surgery.

“Surgery addresses the damaged joint, but patients still need strength to regain mobility and participate in rehabilitation afterward,” indicates Kaylee LeCavalier, PT, DPT, SCS, CSCS, CAPS, a physical therapist and board-certified sports specialist.

Here’s how early to start prehab, how often to do it, and the four moves that LeCavalier recommends before surgery.

In a recent development, “Building strength takes time, and starting earlier provides more opportunity to progressively increase resistance and improve physical capacity before surgery,” explains LeCavalier. “Research suggests benefits in programs lasting 6 to 8 weeks, but no optimal duration has been established.”.

If your surgery is closer than that, don’t dismiss the benefits of doing prehab. “Even with only a few weeks available, patients can still make meaningful progress toward preparing their bodies for surgery and recovery,” LeCavalier says.

For most people, LeCavalier recommends doing strength training two to three days per week, and allowing for proper recovery between more intense sessions. However, how often you should train depends on your beginning strength, activity level, pain, and how well you tolerate the exercises.

Sources indicate that bodyweight exercises are an excellent starting point if you have significant pain or limited strength in your knees or hips. As the moves get easier, you can add weights, use stronger resistance bands or progress to harder variations. A good sign that you’re ready to progress is when you can consistently complete the sets and reps with proper form and control and without a significant increase in pain or swelling during exercise or the following day.

Your hip abductors help stabilize your pelvis when you stand on one leg, which is essential for walking and climbing stairs.

Step-ups focus on one leg at a time, which can help improve mobility and strength in your hips and knees.

Industry observers note that electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you do not write for other people, stop reading this now.

When I was at Snowflake, one of the coolest things that everybody did was this etiquette thing. The first sentence of each email would be “If you don’t develop in this specific part of the code, you can stop reading.” or “If you’re not part of the finance org, you can stop reading.”.

Industry observers note that this made me think a lot about what it means to write for other people. You need to be subservient to your audience. Similarly, thinking about how much space you take is very important. For Slack/Teams threads, you would start with a 3- to 5-line introduction to your topic, and then people could find more details inside the threads.

Recent findings suggest that when I see people writing 2,000 words with content about things that may not apply to everybody, it just makes me sad. Especially when they’re not brief enough. It’s a waste of your readers’ eyes.

So please be kind to your readers.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The new terms take effect on 16 December.
  • Etsy and its “third party partners and vendors” may use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”.
  • Several sellers who had run shops for years noted they were leaving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The new terms take effect on 16 December. They let Etsy and its partners use sellers’ content to build and train AI. The previous version had no clause about AI, the Times reported. The key line reads:.

Etsy and its “third party partners and vendors” may use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”.

Several sellers who had run shops for years noted they were leaving. Illustrator Aaron Millard said on Instagram he was deleting the shop he had run for nearly a decade. He wrote that sellers had no way to opt out.

Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus deleted their shop too. They have sold home goods and stationery on Etsy for 13 years as Cognitive Surplus.

“For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus told the Times.

James Ossman, Etsy’s vice president for customer operations, answered sellers in a post on Etsy’s website this week.

Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote.

Sources indicate that he said third parties get access to sellers’ content for uses such as fraud detection and advertising. In a statement to the Times, he said Etsy would send sellers the revised terms soon. Sellers’ creative work belongs to them, he added.

In a recent development, some critics doubt the reassurance. Tyler Wilde, PC Gamer’s US editor-in-chief, wrote an opinion piece on the clause. To him, it reads like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. He argued that Etsy should leave every seller out of AI training by default.

It has been revealed that etsy has faced seller protests before. In 2022, more than 20,000 sellers went on strike over a fee rise. Etsy had raised its basic sales fee from 5% to 6.5%. In October, it tightened its rules on low-quality AI content after customers complained, the Times reported.

In a recent development, the company cut 12% of its staff in August. The dispute also lands amid wider pushback against AI. Donald Trump Jr told Axios this week that investors had underestimated the AI backlash. Elton John urged Australia to protect artists from AI at the Aria awards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, unveiled the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.

In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has looks to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.

See all results for used Toyota for sale near 97229.

The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.

The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are noted to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.

“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”.

ChatGPT might be the first name that comes to mind when you think of AI, but Anthropic’s Claude has been building a compelling collection of features that could convince even longtime ChatGPT consumers to switch.

With Anthropic now a publicly traded company, more people are likely to discover Claude for themselves. And while both chatbots can help you write emails, analyze documents and tackle everyday tasks, Claude has some clever tricks that set it apart.

I've spent considerable time using both AI assistants, and what makes Claude particularly interesting right now is how it fits into the tools and routines you already use.

Here are five things worth trying.

One of the most underrated reasons to download Claude on your iPhone is how well it works with Apple's native apps.

Through its iOS integrations, Claude can add items to your existing Apple Reminders lists, draft calendar events and prepare text messages and emails.

Imagine planning Thanksgiving dinner with Claude. Once you've settled on a menu, you can ask the chatbot to add the ingredients to your grocery list in Reminders. There's no need to copy and paste everything into another app.

Although ChatGPT has its own scheduled reminders and integrates with Apple Intelligence, Claude offers more direct access to Apple Reminders through its mobile app.

Give it a try with a prompt like: "Blueprint five easy weeknight dinners for my family and add the ingredients to my grocery list in Apple Reminders.".

If you've been using ChatGPT for years, switching to another AI assistant can feel like starting a new job where nobody knows you.

Industry observers note that anthropic has a clever solution. Claude offers a dedicated memory import feature that helps you transfer personal preferences, professional details and other information from competing chatbots.

According to recent reports, claude provides a prompt that you can paste into your existing AI assistant. Once it generates a summary of what it knows about you, simply copy the response into Claude's memory settings.

Industry observers note that you won't transfer your entire conversation history, but you can give Claude a substantial head start. And you don't need a paid subscription to try it.

Both ChatGPT and Claude now offer Skills, which are essentially reusable sets of instructions that teach AI how to perform specific tasks.

However, Claude has an advantage when it comes to bringing those instructions into the applications you already use for work.

The custom Skills you enable in Claude are also available through its Microsoft 365 add-ins for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

You could teach Claude how you like your business proposals formatted, how you organize monthly expenses or how you respond to customer emails. And rather than explaining your preferences every time you open a newly introduced document, Claude can follow the instructions you've already established.

ChatGPT also supports Skills in some Office experiences, but Claude's integration spans all four applications.

Perhaps the most fascinating development in AI right now is that you don't necessarily need to write a prompt to teach a chatbot something upcoming.

With Claude's workflow recording feature, Mac customers can demonstrate a task while Claude captures their screen, mouse clicks, keyboard activity and optional voice narration.

Claude then turns the demonstration into a reusable Skill that you can review and save.

Think about all those little tasks you do on your computer every week. Maybe you organize receipts, upgrade a spreadsheet or compile information from several websites.

Instead of writing detailed instructions for an AI assistant, you can show Claude how you normally do the work.

OpenAI offers similar functionality through Codex's Record & Replay feature, but Claude makes this approach available through its general-purpose desktop assistant.

ChatGPT is excellent at generating images, but Claude takes a different approach to creative work.

Through its design tools, you can give Claude your existing logos, fonts, color palettes and design guidelines to establish a reusable visual identity.

You don't need to be a professional designer to appreciate the possibilities.

If you're starting a small business, running an Etsy shop or launching a newsletter, Claude can help establish a consistent look across your marketing materials, presentations and websites.

Rather than uploading the same reference images and explaining your preferred aesthetic every time, you can work from an established design system that Claude applies across projects.

ChatGPT can follow brand guidelines and reference templates, but Claude's dedicated design system offers a more structured approach to maintaining visual consistency.

I'm not giving up ChatGPT anytime soon, particularly when it comes to image generation and voice conversations. But Claude has become much more than an alternative chatbot for writing and coding.

Anthropic's approach to AI is particularly appealing if you want an assistant that adapts to the way you already work, rather than having to change your habits to accommodate your AI.

If you've never tried Claude, start with the free version. You might be surprised by how much it can do.

Industry News: Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, stated last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In a recent development, in fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

In a recent development, the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is a supremely affordable soundbar that doesn’t compromise on performance. It’s easily one of the best bang-for-buck soundbars I’ve ever tested, and at $119, I can’t quite believe the price.

Some bass-heavy scenes can push dialogue back.

Recent findings suggest that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Price: 5/5Sound quality: 4.5/5Design: 4/5Features: 5/5Overall score: 4.5/5Best for: Upgraders on a budget.

When a soundbar is this cheap, it can feel too good to be true. With an MSRP os $119, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar definitely falls into that category. How can it be one of the best soundbars when it costs less than a monthly cellphone subscription?

It has been revealed that the answer is: I’m not sure. I genuinely doubt Amazon is making a profit on this soundbar.

Industry observers note that for something this inexpensive, bass is surprisingly competent, and it has a dedicated dialogue mode on top of two EQs for music and movies. I never struggled to make out dialogue, even in action-heavy scenes, which is something the TV Soundbar’s substantial brother, the TV Soundbar Plus, struggled with.

So, might the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar be the budget model for you? To find out, keep reading this Amazon Fire TV Soundbar review.

24 inches x 2.5 inches x 3.5 inches.

The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar has a lot going for it: namely its supremely affordable MSRP and surprisingly deft sound.

It has been revealed that the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is $119 at Amazon U.S. and £119 at Amazon U.K. — this is incredibly cheap for a soundbar, let alone a soundbar that sounds this good. And, it's down to $74 for Black Friday.

I’ve also tested the $67 Majority Naga 60 and the $119 Sony HT-S100F, but I’d recommend the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar over both of these due to its superior bass.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Now, let’s get one thing straight. The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar will not, and does not, sound like its more expensive brethren. Want Sonos Ray ($219) or Bose TV Speaker 2nd Gen ($299) quality? It’s not here.

However, this is an $119 soundbar. That’s it. For the price of a monthly cellphone bill, you get a soundbar. And while it doesn’t have the same detail or controlled bass you’d expect on a premium model, that’s okay. That’s not what the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is, and that’s fine.

Even so, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar still sounds better than TV speakers — and that’s all it’s trying to be.

I always test soundbars with 4K Blu-rays, basic-tier Netflix, and music via Bluetooth or AirPlay (connectivity dependent). To test the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar, I watched “Top Gun: Maverick,” “K-Pop Demon Hunters” and “The Batman” on 4K Blu-ray.

In a recent development, “Top Gun: Maverick”’is opening scene is a goldmine for speaker testing. There are all these different sounds fighting for attention: the iconic pulsing bassline in “Danger Zone,” high-frequency in-scene effects like whooshing ropes and clinking metal, and overpowering sounds like jet engines taking off.

Industry observers note that I could hear the propulsive bass in “Danger Zone,” which didn’t overpower the jet engines. While there was a little tinniness at the top of the high-end, I really didn’t mind this in the grand scheme of things. The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar performed admirably.

Dialogue was also clear, even in radioed dialogue scenes. While deep voices, like Tom Cruise’s, caused a little rumbling, I could still understand all dialogue.

Recent findings suggest that “KPop Demon Hunters” also sounded strong: despite a little tinniness in some of the in-movie songs’ percussion, dialogue was particularly exceptional. Bass in the soundtrack was powerful, and diegetic sounds like slamming doors came through well.

It has been revealed that afterwards, I watched “The Batman,” which is a challenging movie for soundbars thanks to the moody dialogue and near-constant rainfall. I could hear every word muttered (yes, muttered; that’s how everyone speaks in this movie). Even footsteps across rainy concrete came through clearly.

It has been revealed that however, loud scenes — like the club scene — pushed dialogue to the back and overpowered the in-scene electronic music, which meant I strained to hear a few of the Penguin’s words. However, I didn’t experience this in any other movie. It’s a Batman thing.

I was extremely surprised and intrigued by this sound quality. It’s miles better than I thought it would be.

According to recent reports, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar has a range of EQ modes: dialogue, movie, music, and you can individually adjust bass. I had to cycle through the EQs to activate each EQ.

Sources indicate that however, the EQs actually improved my viewing experience. I switched between “dialogue” and “movie” while watching “Top Gun”; movie increased bass; dialogue — ever-so surprisingly — clarified dialogue. Music made speech a little too sharp, but obviously, watching a movie in “music” mode is very much "play stupid games, win stupid prizes".

In a recent development, you can even listen to music via Bluetooth, but I wouldn’t write home about this. It would do in a pinch, but the percussion was tinny and the soundbar narrowed the soundstage. It’s fine, but I would just listen to music on one of the best speakers, like the JBL Flip 7.

It’s great to have these options on such a budget-friendly soundbar.

There’s very little I dislike about this soundbar, hence the 4.5-star rating.

It has been revealed that I feel almost unfair marking this as a con, but Amazon kind of brought it upon itself by giving the soundbar DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio. There is no Dolby Atmos or any kind of surround sound. You only really find DTS Virtual:X on select DVDs, so you’ll need to ensure you buy compatible discs to really benefit from this.

Dolby Atmos content — like premium Netflix or Disney+ — will not play as true surround sound because the soundbar is physically incapable of it. If you want spatial audio, you'll have to go for the slightly more expensive Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus.

This is an incredibly cheap soundbar. I really don’t know how Amazon is making a profit on it, if it is at all. At $119, there’s really not much competition.

The only soundbar that comes close is the $119 Sony HT-S100F, which is one of the best cheap soundbars on the market. However, the Sony’s bass is a little lackluster. While the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar’s bass can be a little rumbly at times, at least it isn’t lackluster. What you prefer will depend on you.

In terms of similarly priced competition… well, that’s kind of it. I’ve also tested the Majority Naga 60, which is incredibly cheap at $67, but it can suffer from pinchy treble and rattling bass.

If you want better-than-TV-speaker sound on a serious budget, there’s only one answer to this question: Yes. Actually, wait, I’ve just thought of another: Heck yes.

It has been revealed that I was extremely surprised by the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar’s sound, and I’m sure you will be, too. After testing some disappointing and overpriced Amazon Fire Ember TVs, I wasn’t expecting much — but the soundbar completely blew me away. It’s room-filling, mostly well-controlled, and has extremely intelligible dialogue.

Industry observers note that it's much better than the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus ($139 on Amazon), whose built-in subwoofer overpowers dialogue in action-heavy scenes. If you have a little more to spend, you might want to look into the Amazon Fire TV Plus with Subwoofer ($229) or the model with Rears ($349).

According to recent reports, however, for those on a serious budget, this is the best option out there. Hands-down.

It has been revealed that with my failed iPhone Duo experiment over, I’m back to using iPhone 18 Pro as my default model. But I still have an iPhone Air around for work, and every time I pick it up, I’m struck by how impressive it remains.

Industry observers note that I used the iPhone Air all of last year and loved it. The main reason I upgraded to an iPhone 18 Pro is the camera system. I have young children at home—including newborn twins—and want to capture the best possible photos before they get older.

iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera has been fantastic, and it’s great having the Telephoto again too.

But I still sorely miss the overall design of the iPhone Air. And it sounds like next year, I could get the best of both models.

Rumors indicate Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models will have a unique latest design featuring a quad-curved display that makes it look bezel-free.

The fresh models are expected to also be a bit slimmer, use curved edges, and possibly even bring back titanium. Leakers say the new design borrows a lot from the iPhone Air’s look.

This sounds like exactly what I’ve been hoping for.

While the ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ certainly won’t—and shouldn’t—be as thin as iPhone Air, if it can slim down a little and adopt several other Air design traits, I suspect it will evoke the same affection the Air has.

But unlike the Air, the latest Pro model will still offer the best camera system in an iPhone (not to mention better battery life).

As a huge fan of the design of the Air, and the functionality of the 18 Pro, Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone model could prove the perfect model for me. And for anyone else not opting for iPhone Duo 2.
